In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Four qualities, whoever has them is a pure hypocrite, and whoever has one of them has in him a quality of hypocrisy until he gives it up: when he speaks he lies, when he makes a covenant he betrays it, when he promises he breaks it, and when he disputes he acts wickedly."

In the same work, from the hadith of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet ﷺ:

"The signs of the hypocrite are three, even if he prays and fasts and claims that he is a Muslim: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays."

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Ibn Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ:

"On the Day of Resurrection a banner will be raised for every treacherous person according to the extent of his treachery, and it will be said: This is the treachery of so-and-so, the son of so-and-so."

In the two Sahihs also, from the hadith of Uqbah ibn Amir, from the Prophet ﷺ:

"The conditions most deserving to be fulfilled are those by which you make lawful the private parts."

In Sunan Abi Dawud, from Abu Rafi', who said:

"Quraysh sent me to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When I saw him, Islam was cast into my heart, so I said: O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I will never return to them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: I do not break a covenant, nor do I hold back messengers, but return to them, and if what is in your heart now remains, then return. He said: So I went, then I came to the Prophet ﷺ and embraced Islam."

In Sahih Muslim, from Hudhaifah, who said: "What prevented me from attending Badr was that I went out, I and my father Husayl, and the disbelievers of Quraysh seized us and said: You intend to go to Muhammad. We said: We do not intend him; we only intend Madinah. So they took from us a covenant of Allah and His pledge that we would return to Madinah and not fight alongside him. We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him of the matter, and he said: Go back; we will fulfil our covenant to them and seek Allah's help against them."

In Sunan Abi Dawud, from Abdullah ibn Amir, who said:

"My mother called me one day while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting in our house, and she said: Come, I will give you something. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: What did you intend to give him? She said: I intended to give him dates. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: If you had not given him anything, a lie would have been recorded against you."

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "There are three whose adversary I will be on the Day of Resurrection: a man who gave in My name and then betrayed, a man who sold a free person and consumed his price, and a man who hired a worker, took full work from him, and did not give him his wage."

"The Prophet ﷺ commanded Umar ibn al-Khattab to fulfil the vow he had made in the Jahiliyyah, concerning his i'tikaf for a night at al-Masjid al-Haram. This was a contract that existed before the Sharia."

(Admonition)

The scholars of evil sat at the gate of Paradise, calling people to it with their words while calling them to the Fire with their deeds. Whenever their words said to the people, "Come hither," their deeds said, "Do not listen to them." Had what they called to been true, they would have been the first to respond to it.

Outwardly they are guides, but in reality they are highwaymen.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 61, verse 5:

He said concerning His righteous believers that they asked Him for steadfastness upon guidance by saying: ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us.﴾

The root of zaygh (deviation) is inclination, and from it comes the expression zaghat al-shams (the sun deviated), meaning it declined.

So izaghat al-qalb (causing the heart to deviate) is turning it away from guidance.

And zaygh of the heart is its inclination away from guidance toward misguidance.

Zaygh is attributed to both the heart and the sight, as the Exalted said: ﴿And when the eyes swerved, and the hearts reached the throats﴾.

Qatadah and Muqatil said: they were fixed in terror (shakhasat faraqan).

This is an approximation of the meaning, for shukhus (fixed staring) is other than zaygh. It is that a person opens his eyes wide, looking at a thing, without blinking.

From this comes the expression shakhasa basar al-mayyit (the eye of the dead person became fixed).

When the sights turned away from everything, and looked only at those who had come against them from every direction, they were occupied and turned away from looking at anything else.

And they were fixed in gazing at the confederates.

Al-Kalbi said: their sights turned away except from looking at them.

Al-Farra' said: they swerved away from everything, and did not turn except toward their enemy, staring bewildered at him.

I say: when the heart is filled with terror, that occupies it from noticing anything other than what is feared, so the sight swerves from settling on other things. And this is its opposite.

(Section)

Abu al-Qasim al-Suhayli and others thought that the Prophet's ﷺ name Ahmad was given before his name Muhammad. They said: "This is why the Messiah gave glad tidings of him by the name Ahmad." In a lengthy hadith about Musa, when he said to his Lord, exalted is He, "I find a nation whose characteristics are such-and-such; make them my nation," He said: "Those are the nation of Ahmad, O Musa." He said: "O Allah, make me one of the nation of Ahmad."

They said: the name Muhammad came in the Qur'an specifically, due to His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds and believe in what has been sent down upon Muhammad﴾ [Muhammad: 2] and His saying ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah﴾ [al-Fath: 29].

On this basis they built that Ahmad is the superlative form derived from the act of the doer, i.e., "the one who praises his Lord the most," while Muhammad is "the one who is praised," whom all creation praises. This name is only realized after its existence and manifestation, for then the people of the heavens and the earth praise him, and on the Day of Resurrection the people of the Gathering praise him. So when he appeared into existence and the good that resulted from his appearance came about, creation praised him with repeated praise; thus his naming as Muhammad was later than his naming as Ahmad.

In this statement there are several objections:

The first: he was named Muhammad before the Gospel. Likewise his name is in the Torah, and every scholar among the believing People of the Book acknowledges this. We will mention the text they have in the Torah and what is the correct interpretation of it.

It says in the Torah concerning Isma'il a statement, whose wording is: "And concerning Isma'il, I have heard you; behold, I have blessed him and made him fruitful, and I will multiply him exceedingly from what is swept away (mimma bad)." This was mentioned after Isma'il was mentioned, and that he would beget twelve great ones, among them a great one whose name would be Mamad Bad. According to the believing scholars among the People of the Book, this is explicit regarding the name of the Prophet ﷺ, Muhammad.

I saw in some commentaries on the Torah, after this text, what is reported: the commentator said: "These two letters in two places include the name of the Master, the Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, because if you consider the letters of the name Muhammad, you find them in the two mentioned words: the two m's of Muhammad correspond to the two m's in the words, and one of the two d's, and the remaining letter of Muhammad, which is the ḥ, corresponds to the remaining letters of the words, which are the b, the two alifs, and the second d."

I say: he means by the two letters the two words. He said: "Because the ḥ, in reckoning, has eight in numerical value, the b has two, each alif has one, and the d has four, so the total is eight, which is the ḥ's share in the total numerical value. Thus the two letters, meaning the two words, Mamad Bad, have explicitly included three-quarters of the name Muhammad ﷺ, and its other quarter is indicated by the remaining letters in writing, in the way you have pointed out."

The commentator said: "If it is asked, what is your basis for this interpretation?"

We say: our basis is the basis of the Jewish scholars in interpreting such ambiguous letters that came in the Torah, like His saying, exalted is He: "O Musa, tell the Children of Israel that each of them should put on the corner of his garment a blue thread having eight tips, and tie in it five knots, and call it ṣīṣīt." The Jewish scholars said: the interpretation and wisdom of this is that whoever sees that blue thread, counts its eight ends and its five knots, and mentions its name, remembers what is obligatory upon him of the obligations of Allah, exalted is He, because Allah imposed on the Children of Israel six hundred and thirteen commandments. For the ṣād and the yā' (in the word) are two hundred, and the tā' is four hundred, so the total of the name is six hundred, and the tips and knots are thirteen. It is as if it says, by its form and name: remember the obligations of Allah, mighty and majestic.

This commentator said: as for the statement of many exegetes that the meaning of these two letters is "jiddan jiddan" (very, very) because the word "mad" came alone in the Torah with the meaning of "jiddan" (very), he said: this is not sound, because of the bā' attached to this letter, for the saying of one who says, "I honor you bajadan," is not straight speech. So when this letter was transmitted from the eternal Torah, which was sent down on tablets of jewel to Kalim (Moses) in the kinonic script, and this letter in it was joined to the bā', it became known that the intended meaning is other than what those who say it means "very" have held, since no interpretation suits it except this explanation. This is supported by His saying, in another place, to Ibrahim about his son Isma'il: that he would beget twelve nobles, and from among the nobles there would be a person named Mimma Bad. The Torah has thus explicitly stated that these two letters are a proper name of a specific noble person from the descendants of Isma'il. Therefore the view of those who say it is a verbal noun for emphasis is invalidated, for the explicit statement that it is a proper name refutes the one who claims it is a noun of meaning. And Allah knows best. End of his words.

Another said: there is no need for this strained effort in explaining his name ﷺ in the Torah; rather, his name in it is clearer than all of this. The Torah is in the Hebrew language, which is close to Arabic, indeed it is the closest of the nations' languages to Arabic. Often the difference between them lies in the manner of articulating letters and pronouncing them, such as emphatic and non-emphatic, damma and fatha, and other things. Consider this from the closeness between the individual words of the two languages. The Arabs say "lā" and the Hebrews say "lo," so they pronounce the lām with a ḍamma and bring an alif between the wāw and the alif. The Arabs say "qudus" and the Hebrews say "qudesh." The Arabs say "anta" and the Hebrews say "ana." The Arabs say "ya'ti kadhā" and the Hebrews say "yoti," pronouncing the yā' with a ḍamma and bringing an alif after it between the wāw and the alif. The Arabs say "qudsuka," and the Hebrews say "qad sha ḥa." The Arabs say "minhu," and the Hebrews say "mimnu." The Arabs say "min Yahudhā," and the Hebrews say "mehudhā." The Arabs say "sami'tuka," and the Hebrews say "shim'eykha." The Arabs say "man," and the Hebrews say "mi." The Arabs say "yamīnuhu," and the Hebrews say "mīnu." The Arabs say "lahu," and the Hebrews say "lo" between the wāw and the alif. Likewise the Arabs say "ummah," and the Hebrews say "ummo." The Arabs say "ard," and the Hebrews say "iyrṣ." The Arabs say "wāḥid," and the Hebrews say "iyḥad." The Arabs say "ʿālim," and the Hebrews say "ʿolām." The Arabs say "kays," and the Hebrews say "kiyes." The Arabs say "ya'kulu," and the Hebrews say "yokhul." The Arabs say "tīn," and the Hebrews say "tiyin." The Arabs say "ilāh," and the Hebrews say "oluh." The Arabs say "ilāhunā," and the Hebrews say "elohinu." The Arabs say "abānā," and the Hebrews say "abotinu." They say "bi-aṣbaʿ Ilohīm," meaning "the finger of God," and they say "mabnum," meaning "the son," and they say "ḥalīb" meaning "ḥalūb" (milked). When they want to say "Do not eat the kid in its mother's milk," they say:

"Lo tokhul le-dhī mā ḥalūb ummo."

And they say "lo [tukalū]," meaning "do not eat." And they call the books "al-mishna," whose meaning in the language of the Arabs is "the repeated one," that is, read again and again.

We will not elaborate more than this on the closeness of the two languages.

Beneath this is a secret understood by one who grasps the closeness between the two nations and the two laws.

And the pairing of the Torah with the Qur'an in more than one place of the Book, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not disbelieved in what was given to Musa before? They said: "Two works of magic supporting each other," and they said: "Indeed, we are disbelievers in all of it." Say: "Then bring a Book from Allah which is better guidance than both of them, that I may follow it, if you are truthful."﴾ [al-Qasas: 48-49]

And His saying in Surat al-An'am, in response to those who said: ﴿Allah has not sent down anything upon a human being." Say: "Who sent down the Book which Musa brought, as light and guidance for the people?"﴾ [al-An'am: 91]

Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿And this is a Book We have sent down, blessed, confirming what is before it﴾ [al-An'am: 92]. And He said at the end of the surah: ﴿Then We gave Musa the Book, complete for the one who did good, and a detailed explanation of everything, and guidance and mercy, that they might believe in the meeting with their Lord. And this is a Book We have sent down, blessed, so follow it and fear Allah, that you may receive mercy.﴾ [al-An'am: 154-155]

And He said at the beginning of Surat Al 'Imran: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. Allah — there is no deity except Him, the Living, the Self-Subsisting. He has sent down upon you the Book in truth, confirming what was before it, and He sent down the Torah and the Gospel before, as guidance for the people.﴾

And He said: ﴿And We had certainly given Musa and Harun the criterion and a light and a reminder for the righteous, who fear their Lord unseen and are apprehensive of the Hour. And this is a blessed reminder which We have sent down; so are you now rejecting it?﴾ [al-Anbiya: 48-50]

For this reason He, exalted is He, mentions the story of Musa, repeats it, reiterates it, and consoles His Messenger ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, when he was harmed by people: "Musa was harmed with more than this, and he was patient."

For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "What was in the Children of Israel will exist in my nation, to the extent that if among them there was one who openly had intercourse with his mother, there would be in this nation one who does the same." So reflect on this correspondence between the two Messengers, the two Books, and the two laws, meaning the correct law that was not altered, and the two nations and the two languages. When you look at the letters of Muhammad and the letters of Mamad Bad, you find the two words are one word: the two m's in them, the hamza and the ḥā' are from one point of articulation, and the d often finds its place as a dhāl in their language; they say "iyḥadh" for "one," and they say "quddhsh" for "the holy" (al-quds). The d and the dhāl are close. Whoever considers the two languages and considers these two names will not doubt that they are one. There are parallels to this in the two languages, such as Musa: in Hebrew it is "Mosha" with a shīn, and its root means water and tree, for they say "mo" for water and "sha" for tree, and Musa was picked up by the household of Pharaoh from between water and tree. The variation between Musa and Mosha is like the variation between Muhammad and Mamad Bad.

Likewise Isma'il, which in their language is "Yishma'el," with a yā' in place of the alif and a shīn in place of the sīn. The difference between them is like the difference between Muhammad and Mamad Bad. Likewise al-'Is, the brother of Ya'qub, they call "'Esau," which is "'Eis." A parallel to this among non-proper words, from what preceded, is His saying "yishma'un," meaning "they hear," and they say "āqīm" with the hamza elongated while pronouncing it with a ḍamma, meaning "aqīm," and they say "mī qārab," meaning "man qārab" (whoever drew near), and "wasaṭ akhīhim," meaning "their brothers." This is something acknowledged by every believing scholar among the People of the Book.

The purpose is that the name of the Prophet ﷺ in the Torah is Muhammad, as it is in the Qur'an. As for the Messiah, he called him Ahmad, as Allah related from him in the Qur'an. Thus, the naming of him as Ahmad occurred after his naming as Muhammad in the Torah and before his naming as Muhammad in the Qur'an, so it fell between the two namings, enclosed by them. It has been established that these two names are in reality adjectives, and their adjectival nature does not negate their being proper names, and their meanings are intended. So each nation knew him by the more familiar of the two descriptors among them. Muhammad is a intensive form (mufa'al) from praise, meaning one whose many qualities are praised repeatedly, praise after praise. This is only known after knowing the qualities of goodness and the kinds of knowledge, insights, morals, attributes, and actions which deserve repeated praise. There is no doubt that the Children of Israel were the first possessors of knowledge and the Book, of which Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We wrote for him on the tablets of everything an admonition and a detailed explanation of all things﴾ [al-A'raf: 145].

For this reason the community of Musa had broader knowledge and understanding than the community of the Messiah. For this reason the Messiah's law is not complete without the Torah and its rulings, for the Messiah, peace be upon him, and his community were bound by its rulings. The Gospel is, as it were, completing it and perfecting its virtues. The Qur'an combines the virtues of both Books.

Thus the Prophet ﷺ was known to this community as Muhammad, who combined the qualities of goodness deserving praise, praise after praise. And he was known to the community of the Messiah as Ahmad, who deserves to be praised more than others are praised, and whose praise is superior to the praise of others. For the community of the Messiah had disciplines, morals, and acts of worship that the community of Musa did not have. For this reason most of their scripture consisted of admonitions, asceticism, morals, and exhortation to kindness, forbearance, and forgiveness. It is even said that laws are of three kinds: a law of justice, which is the Torah, containing judgment and retaliation; a law of grace, which is the Gospel, containing pardon, noble morals, forgiveness, and kindness, like His saying: "Whoever takes your cloak, give him your robe too; whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him the left; and whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two." And the law of our Prophet combined both, and it is the law of the Qur'an, for it mentions justice and makes it obligatory, and grace and encourages it, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it, but whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with Allah. Indeed, He does not love wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Shura: 40]. So his name came to this community with the superlative form (af'al al-tafdil), indicating excellence and perfection, just as their law came with the excess that completes the Torah's law. And it came in the Book that combines the virtues of the Books before it, with both names together. So reflect on this section, and clarify the connection between meanings and their names and their suitability for them. And all praise is due to Allah, who bestows favor by His grace and guidance.

As for Abu al-Qasim's statement that the name Muhammad was realized only after his appearance into existence, because then he was praised with repeated praise, the same applies to Muhammad as well. As for his statement about the name Ahmad, that it preceded because he is the one who praises his Lord most, and this precedes creation's praise of him, this is a construction based on the view that it is a superlative from the act of the doer. But according to the other, sound view, this does not arise. This has been established previously. And Allah, glory be to Him, knows best.

(Section: On the impossibility of believing in any prophet at all while denying the prophethood of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that whoever denies his prophethood is more denying of the prophethood of other prophets)

This becomes clear from several aspects:

**First**, the prophets who came before him foretold his prophethood and commanded their peoples to believe in him, as has already been mentioned. Whoever denies his prophethood has denied the prophets before him in what they reported, and has opposed them in what they enjoined, namely belief in him. So affirming him is a necessary consequence of affirming them. When the necessary consequence is negated, the thing that necessitates it is negated with certainty. The proof of this necessary connection is the many aspects already mentioned, which together establish with certainty that he (ﷺ) was mentioned in the divine books on the tongues of the prophets. When the necessary connection is established, the negation of the consequent necessitates the negation of what it follows from.

**Second**: The call of Muhammad ibn Abdullah (ﷺ), may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, is the call of all the messengers before him, from the first of them to the last.

Whoever rejects his call therefore rejects the call of all his brother prophets, for all the messengers came with what he came with. If the one who rejects him claims that what he brought is false, he has rejected every messenger Allah sent and every book He revealed. It is impossible to believe that what he brought is true while he is a liar who fabricates against Allah. This is perfectly clear. It is like witnesses who testify to the truth, and the opponent confirms them and says: "These are all upright and truthful witnesses." Then another witness testifies to exactly the same testimony, and the opponent says: "This testimony is false and a lie, without any basis." That is certainly a rejection of the testimony of all the witnesses. His acknowledgment that their testimony is sound, and that it is a testimony of truth, does not save him from having rejected them, nor does it help him if he claims the one who gave the latter testimony is lying about what he testified to.

Just as, if Muhammad (ﷺ) had not appeared, the prophethoods of the prophets before him would have been invalidated, so too if he is not affirmed, there is no affirmation of any prophet before him.

**Third**: The signs and proofs that establish the soundness of his prophethood and his truthfulness are many times over the signs of the messengers before him. For no prophet has a sign that obliges belief in him except that Muhammad (ﷺ) has its equivalent, or something equivalent to it in its indication, even if it is not of the same kind.

The signs of Muhammad's prophethood are greater, mightier, more dazzling and more indicative. And knowledge of their transmission is certain, because the period is close, the transmitters are numerous, they lived in different cities and different eras, and it is impossible for them to have conspired to lie. So knowledge of the signs of his prophethood is like knowledge of his very existence, his appearance and his city, to the extent that stubborn denial of it is not possible. Whoever stubbornly denies it is exceedingly shameless and deceitful, like someone who stubbornly denies the existence of things that people have witnessed but he himself has not seen, such as cities, regions, mountains and rivers.

If it is permissible to cast doubt on all of that, then casting doubt on the existence of Moses and Jesus and the signs of their prophethood is even more permissible. And if casting doubt on those two and the signs of their prophethood is forbidden, then forbidding it regarding Muhammad (ﷺ) and the signs of his prophethood is even stronger. For this reason, when some of the scholars of the People of the Book realized that belief in Moses cannot be complete while rejecting Muhammad, they disbelieved in all of them and said: ﴿Allah has not sent down anything upon a human being.﴾

As Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They did not estimate Allah with the true estimation when they said: "Allah has not sent down anything upon a human being." Say: "Who sent down the Book that Moses brought, a light and guidance for the people, which you make into scrolls, showing some and concealing much? And you were taught what neither you nor your fathers knew." Say: "Allah." Then leave them in their discourse, playing.﴾

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: A Jewish man called Malik ibn al-Sayf came and disputed with the Prophet (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "I adjure you by the One who sent down the Torah to Moses: do you not find in the Torah that Allah hates the fat rabbi?" He was a fat rabbi. The enemy of Allah became angry and said: "By Allah, Allah has not sent down anything upon a human being." His companions with him said: "Woe to you, not even Moses?" He said: "By Allah, Allah has not sent down anything upon a human being." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿They did not estimate Allah with the true estimation when they said: "Allah has not sent down anything upon a human being. Say: 'Who sent down the Book...'"﴾ and the verses that follow. This is also the view of Ikrimah.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: Some Jews came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was sitting with his knees raised and his arms wrapped around them, and they said: "O Abu al-Qasim, will you not bring us a book from the heavens, as Moses brought tablets carried from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?" So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿The People of the Book ask you to bring down a book upon them from the heaven. They had asked Moses for something greater than that, when they said: "Show us Allah plainly."﴾ up to the end of the verse.

Then a Jewish man fell onto his knees and said: "Allah has not sent down anything upon a human being." In another wording: "Allah has not sent down anything upon you, nor upon Moses, nor upon Jesus, nor upon anyone at all. Allah has not sent down anything upon a human being." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) untied his arms from around his knees and began saying: "Not even upon anyone?"

Mujahid and a group of others held that the verse was revealed concerning the polytheists of Quraysh. They are the ones who denied the very foundation of messengerhood and disbelieved in the messengers. As for the People of the Book, they did not deny the prophethood of Moses and Jesus. This is the view chosen by Ibn Jarir, who said: "It is the most correct of the opinions, because it fits the context of the report about them. It is more appropriate that it be a report about them rather than about the Jews, since no mention of the Jews has preceded it in a way that connects with this report concerning those whom Allah reports about in this verse, when they denied that Allah sent down any of the books upon a human being. That is not the creed of the Jews. Rather, the well-known position of the Jews is the affirmation of the scrolls of Abraham, Moses and the Psalms of David. The report from the beginning of the surah up to this point is a report about the polytheists who worship idols. And the words ﴿They did not estimate Allah with the true estimation﴾ are connected to what precedes them and not separated from it."

I say: What strengthens his view is that the surah is Meccan. So it is a report about the heretics of the Arabs who deny the very foundation of prophethood. However, a question remains: How is it fitting to refute them with what they do not acknowledge, namely the sending down of the Book that Moses brought? And how can it be said to them, "which you make into scrolls, showing some and concealing much," especially on the reading of the one who reads with the second-person ta'? Is that suitable for anyone other than the Jews? For they used to conceal from the Book whatever did not agree with their desires and purposes, and display other parts of it. This is like what Ibn Suriya did when the Torah was brought into the assembly of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to cite the text of the Torah concerning the ruling on stoning. He placed his hand over it and read what came before and after it, while Ibn Salam exposed his deception.

Since they were like this, Allah argued against them with what they acknowledge of the Book of Moses. Then He rebuked them for betraying Allah and His Messenger, for concealing part of it and displaying part of it.

This is a digression from the mention of their total denial of prophethood, which is itself a concealing and hiding, to the denial of what they acknowledged their own book to contain, by concealing and hiding it. That is a known disposition of theirs that cannot be denied. For whoever conceals part of his book, which he acknowledges to be from Allah, how would he not deny the very foundation of prophethood?

Then Allah argued against them by pointing out that they had come to know through revelation what neither they nor their fathers knew, and that had it not been for the revelation which Allah sent down to His prophets and messengers, they would not have reached that knowledge. Then He commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to answer this question, which is His saying: ﴿Who sent down the Book that Moses brought?﴾

So He said: ﴿Say: "Allah,"﴾ meaning: Allah is the One who sent it down. In other words, if they disbelieve in it and deny it, then you, [O Muhammad], affirm it and acknowledge it, and ﴿leave them in their discourse, playing.﴾

The answer to this question may be given as follows, and Allah knows best: Allah, glorified and exalted, argued against them with what the People of the Book acknowledge, and they are the people of knowledge, unlike the nations that have no book. In other words: if you deny the very foundation of prophethood, and that Allah sent down anything upon a human being, then here is the Book of Moses, which the People of the Book acknowledge, and they know more than you. So ask them about it.

There are many parallels to this in the Qur'an, in which Allah the Glorified calls upon the People of the Book as witnesses against the deniers of prophethood and of monotheism. The meaning is: if you deny that Allah has sent down anything upon a human being, then who sent down the Book of Moses? If you do not know that, then ask the People of the Book.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿which you make into scrolls, showing some and concealing much,﴾ whoever reads it with the ya' (third person) is reporting about the Jews using the form of absence. Whoever reads it with the ta' (second person) is addressing this class of people who did that, saying: "You make it..." O you to whom it was revealed in this manner. This is one of the signs of his prophethood (ﷺ), that he informs the People of the Book of what they had done with their book, that they made it into scrolls, displayed part of it and concealed much of it. This could not be known except through a revelation from Allah the Exalted.

It is not necessary that His saying ﴿which you make into scrolls﴾ be addressed to those about whom it was reported that they said: ﴿Allah has not sent down anything upon a human being.﴾ Rather, this is a digression from one thing to its counterpart, its like and its implication. There are many parallels to this in the Qur'an.

Furthermore, these people could not complete their denial of the prophethood of the Prophet (ﷺ) and their stubborn rejection except by this general denial and rejection. They saw that if they acknowledged some prophethoods and denied his prophethood, their contradiction and their discrimination between two alike would become evident, and that they could not believe in a prophet while denying the prophethood of one whose prophethood is more manifest and whose signs are greater than those of the one they acknowledged.

Allah the Glorified informed us that whoever denies that He has sent His messengers and revealed His books has not estimated Him with the true estimation, and has attributed to Him what is not fitting for Him, whereas He is exalted and far above that. For in that there is a denial of His lordship, His divinity, His dominion, His wisdom and His mercy, and an evil assumption about Him: that He created His creation in vain and falsehood, and that He left them neglected and unguided. This contradicts His perfect perfection, and He is exalted above everything that contradicts His perfection. Whoever denies His speech, His addressing of His creation, and His sending of messengers to His creation has not estimated Him as He should be estimated, and has not known Him as He should be known, nor magnified Him as He should be magnified. Just as whoever worships another god alongside Him has not estimated Him as He should be estimated, and is a nullifier and denier of His attributes of perfection, the qualities of His majesty, the sending of His messengers, and the sending down of His books, and has not magnified Him as He should be magnified.

For this reason, the denial of the prophethood of the seal of the prophets and messengers, and the rejection of him, amount in reality to a denial of the Lord, the Exalted, and a repudiation of Him. It is impossible to affirm His lordship, His divinity and His dominion, indeed even His existence, while rejecting Muhammad ibn Abdullah (ﷺ). We have already pointed to this in the debate that preceded. Disbelief in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) does not combine with affirming the Lord, the Exalted, and His attributes at all, just as disbelief in the Return and the Last Day does not combine with affirming the existence of the Creator at all.

As for the Christians, you already know what they grasped of their Worshipped One and what they attributed to Him, and what they said about their prophet, and how they never truly grasped his reality. They described Allah with some of the greatest defects and deficiencies, and they described His servant and messenger with what is not his in any respect. They did not know Allah or His messenger. As for the Return, which they affirmed, they did not grasp its reality, and they did not believe in what the messengers brought of the truth, for in their view there is no eating in Paradise, no drinking, and no spouses there, nor wide-eyed maidens with whom men take pleasure as they do in this world. Nor did they know the reality of their own souls, what makes them happy and what makes them wretched. Whoever does not know that is most unlikely to know the reality of anything as it should be known at all.

Thus they knew neither their own souls, nor the One who originated them and brought them into being, nor the one whom Allah made a means of their salvation and happiness, nor the existents, that all of them are needy, lordly-ruled, created, and that every rational being among them, human, jinn and angel, and everyone in the heavens and the earth, is His servant and possession, created, made, sustained, needy in every respect. Whoever does not know this does not know anything.

The Jews, may Allah curse them, Allah has related to you the ignorance of their forefathers, their worship of the calf, and their misguidance, which indicates what lies beyond them of the darkness of ignorance, layer upon layer. Their worship of the calf that their own hands fashioned from gold is sufficient evidence of this. And from their stupidity and dullness, they made it in the likeness of the most foolish of animals, the least intelligent, which is proverbially cited for lack of understanding. Consider this ignorance and stupidity, which exceed all bounds: how they worshipped another god besides Allah, though they had witnessed proofs of Divine Oneness and of the greatness and majesty of the Lord that no one else had witnessed!

Since they resolved to take a god besides Allah, they took one while their prophet was alive among them. They did not wait for his death!

Since they did this, they did not take it from among the honoured angels or the living, speaking beings, but took it from inanimate matter! And since they did this, they did not make it from the heavenly substances like the sun, the moon and the stars, but from earthly substances! And since they did this, they did not take it from the substances that are created above the earth and高 above it, like the mountains and the like, but from substances that exist only beneath the earth, while rocks and stones are above them! And since they did this, they did not take it from a substance that needs no craftsmanship, the introduction of fire, turning it into various shapes, striking it with iron and smelting it, but from a substance that requires the hands to handle it in various ways, the introduction into fire, burning and extracting its impurities. And since they did this, they did not fashion it in the image of a noble angel, nor of a sent prophet, nor in the image of a heavenly substance that hands cannot reach, but in the image of an earthly animal. And since they did this, they did not fashion it in the likeness of the noblest and strongest animals, the most resistant to injustice, such as the lion and the elephant and the like, but fashioned it in the image of the most stupid of animals, the most submissive to oppression and humiliation, one that is made to plough the earth and is watered by irrigation channels and water-wheels, and has no strength by which it can defend itself against anyone, great or small.

What knowledge, then, do these people have of their object of worship, their prophet, and the realities of existent things?

It is fitting that one who asked his prophet to make for him a god, and who worshipped idols as a made-up god, after witnessing those dazzling signs, should not know the reality of God, nor His names, attributes, descriptions and religion, nor the reality of the created being and its need and poverty. Had these people known their object of worship and their messenger, they would not have said to their prophet, "We will not believe in you until we see Allah openly," nor would they have said to him, "So go, you and your Lord, and fight."

Nor would they have killed a soul and cast the slain man at the doors of the innocent to escape responsibility for his killing, while their prophet was alive among them, and news from heaven and revelation came to him morning and evening. It is as though they supposed that this could be hidden from Allah just as it is hidden from people!

Had they known their object of worship, they would not have said in some of their address to him, "O our father, wake up from your sleep, do not sleep!"

Had they known Him, they would not have hastened to wage war against His prophets, to kill them, imprison them and exile them, nor would they have devised tricks to make lawful what He had forbidden and to annul His obligations by all kinds of stratagems.

The Torah has testified to their lack of intelligence and that they are among the stupid.

(Section)

It is absolutely impossible for a Jew to believe in the prophethood of Moses, peace be upon him, unless he believes in the prophethood of Muhammad, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him. And it is impossible for a Christian to acknowledge the prophethood of Jesus except after acknowledging the prophethood of Muhammad, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him.

The explanation of this is that it may be said to these two communities: You did not witness these two messengers, nor did you witness their signs and the proofs of their prophethood. How, then, can a rational person accept the lie of a prophet who has a prior call, an established word, dazzling signs, and the confirmation of one who is not like him, nor near him in this? Because no one saw either of the two prophets nor witnessed their miracles. So if he denies the prophethood of one of them, he is bound to deny the prophethood of both. And if he affirms one of them, he is bound to affirm the prophethood of both. Whoever disbelieves in one prophet has disbelieved in all the prophets, and his belief in him will not benefit him.

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, and wish to make a distinction between Allah and His messengers, and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and wish to adopt a way between that—those are the disbelievers, truly. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment. And those who believe in Allah and His messengers and do not make distinction between any of them—those, He will soon give them their rewards. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [An-Nisa 150-152]. And He, the Exalted, says: ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been revealed to him from his Lord, and the believers. Each believes in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers. We make no distinction between any of His messengers﴾ [Al-Baqarah 285].

So we say to the one who has earned wrath: Have you seen Moses and witnessed his miracles? He will necessarily say: No.

We say to him: By what did you know his prophethood and his truthfulness?

He has two answers.

The first: that he says, "My father informed me of that and told me about it."

The second: that he says, "Mass transmission (tawatur) and the testimony of nations have established that for me, just as their testimony established for me the existence of distant lands, seas, and well-known rivers, even though I have not seen them."

If he chooses the first answer and says, "My father's testimony and his informing me of Moses' prophethood is the cause of my believing in him," we say to him: Why was your father truthful in that in your view, protected from lying? You see that unbelievers are taught by their fathers what is disbelief in your view. So if you see false religions and corrupt doctrines taken by their adherents from their fathers, just as you took your creed from your father, and you know that what they follow is misguidance, then it is necessary for you to examine what you took from your father, lest your case be like theirs.

If he says, "What I took from my father is more sound than what people took from their fathers," his saying is countered by others' like claims.

If he says, "My father is more truthful than their fathers, more knowledgeable, and more excellent," all people counter him with similar claims about their fathers.

If he says, "I know my father's condition, and I do not know the condition of others," it is said to him: What assures you that someone other than your father is not more truthful than your father, and more truthful, and more knowledgeable?

In any case: if imitating his father is a sound proof, then imitating others' fathers is likewise. And if that is invalid, then imitating his own father is invalid.

If he retracts this answer and chooses the second answer, saying, "I knew Moses' prophethood through mass transmission, generation after generation. They reported his appearance, his miracles, his signs, and the proofs of his prophethood which compel me to believe in him," it is said to him: This answer does not benefit you, for you have invalidated what mass transmission established regarding the prophethood of Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them both.

If you say: "The appearance of Moses, his miracles and signs were transmitted by mass transmission, but this was not transmitted regarding Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them both," it is said to you: This is what is fitting for the stupefaction of the people of wrath. For all nations know that you are a people of slander. Otherwise, it is well known that those who transmitted the miracles of Jesus and Muhammad, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon them, are many times more numerous than you. And the miracles that their earliest followers witnessed are no less than the miracles that Moses, peace be upon him, brought, and they were transmitted from them by people of mass transmission, generation after generation, century after century.

You do not accept the report of mass transmission in this matter and reject it, so it is necessary for you not to accept it in the matter of Moses, peace be upon him.

It is known necessarily that whoever affirms one thing and denies its like has contradicted himself.

When a prophet becomes famous in one age, and his prophethood is validly established in that age by the signs that appeared upon him to the people of his age, and his news reaches the people of another age, it is obligatory upon them to affirm him and believe in him. Moses, Muhammad and Jesus are equal in this. Perhaps the mass testimony for Moses' prophethood is weaker than the mass testimony for the prophethood of Jesus and Muhammad, because the people of wrath have been torn apart by Allah, the Exalted, in every direction, scattered throughout the earth, and stripped of their kingdom and honour, so they have no life except under the domination of other nations over them. This is unlike the community of Jesus, peace be upon him, for they have spread throughout the earth, and there are kings among them, and they possess kingdoms.

As for the Hunafa' (the upright monotheists, i.e., the Muslims), their kingdoms have spanned the eastern and western regions of the earth, and they have filled the world, plains and mountains. How, then, could their transmission of what they transmitted be false, while the transmission of the people of wrath, the sluggish, few, and transient, be true?

Thus it is established that no Jew on the face of the earth can believe in the prophethood of Moses, peace be upon him, except by affirming and acknowledging the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). And no Christian can at all believe in Jesus, peace be upon him, except after believing in Muhammad, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him.

Nor does the testimony of the Muslims to the prophethood of Moses and Jesus benefit these two communities, because they believed in them through the hand of Muhammad, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, and their belief in them was part of belief in Muhammad and in what he brought. Had it not been for him, we would not have known their prophethood, nor would we have believed in them.

Moreover, the people of wrath and misguidance do not possess from their prophets anything that necessitates belief in them. Had it not been for the Qur'an and Muhammad, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, we would not have known anything of the signs of the earlier prophets.

Thus Muhammad, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, and his book are what established the prophethood of Moses and the prophethood of Jesus, not the Jews nor the Christians.

Rather, his very appearance and coming was a confirmation of their prophethood. For they informed of his appearance and gave glad tidings of him before he appeared. So when he was sent, his mission was a confirmation of them both.

This is one of the two meanings in the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And they say, "Shall we indeed leave our gods for a mad poet?" Nay, he has brought the truth and confirmed the messengers﴾ [As-Saffat 36-37].

That is, his coming is a confirmation of them from two angles:

From the angle of their informing of his coming and his mission, and from the angle of his informing of the like of what they informed, and the correspondence of what he brought with what they brought. For when an earlier messenger brings a matter that is known only through revelation, and then another prophet comes who was not contemporary with him, nor in the same place, and did not receive from him what he brought, and informs of exactly the same as the first, this proves the truthfulness of both the first and the last messengers. This is like two men, one of whom reports a matter from direct observation, and then another comes from a different land and region, such that it is known he did not meet him, nor receive from him, nor from anyone who received from him, and he reports exactly what the first reported. The hearer is compelled to affirm both the first and the second.

The second meaning: he did not come denying those prophets before him, disparaging them, as kings who dominate people do with the kings before them. Rather, he came confirming them, testifying to their prophethood. Had he been a liar, fabricating from his own mind a policy, he would not have confirmed those before him; rather, he would have disparaged them and reviled them, as the enemies of the prophets do.

(Another section)

He said in (Hidayat al-Hayara):

We shall show them that they cannot establish for the Messiah any virtue, prophethood, sign or miracle except by acknowledging that Muhammad (ﷺ) is the Messenger of Allah. Otherwise, with their denial of him, it is absolutely impossible for anything of that to be established for the Messiah. So we say: If you, assemblies of the Trinitarians, worshippers of the cross, disbelieve in the Qur'an and Muhammad (ﷺ), then from where do you have the means to establish for Jesus any virtue or miracle?

And who transmitted to you any sign or miracle from him? You only followed those who came after him, more than two hundred and tens of years later. You reported a dream that was seen and rushed to affirm it. It would have been more fitting for one who disbelieves in the Qur'an to deny the existence of Jesus in the world, since he does not accept the words of the Jews about him, especially as they are his greatest enemies, who accused him and his mother of great calumnies. The reports about the Messiah and the cross, your sheikhs in them are the Jews, may Allah curse them, and they disagree among themselves about his affair with the greatest disagreement, and you disagree with them about his affair.

For the Jews, may Allah curse them, claim that when they seized him and imprisoned him for forty days, they said: It was not permitted for you to imprison him for more than three days, then kill him; but he was supported by one of the commanders of the Romans, because he was intimate with him in the art of medicine among them.

And in the Gospel that is in your hands, it is said that he was seized on the morning of Friday and crucified at the ninth hour of the same day. So when do you agree with the Jews about his report?

The Jews are unanimous that no miracle appeared for him, and no sign was manifested from him to them, except that he flew one day, and they intended to seize him, and another of them flew after him, overtook him in his flight, and he fell to the earth, according to their claim.

And in the Gospel that is in your hands, in more than one place, there is what testifies that he had no miracle and no sign. Among that is that it is explicitly stated that the Jews said to him one day: "What will you do, that we may end with him the matter of Allah?" He said: "That you believe in the one who sent him." They said to him: "What is your sign that you show us, so that we may believe in you, and you know that our fathers ate the manna and the quails in the wilderness?" He said: "If Moses gave you bread, I give you heavenly bread," meaning the bliss of the Hereafter. Had they known a miracle for him, they would not have said that.

And in the Gospel that is in your hands, the Jews said to him: "What is the sign by which we may believe you?" He said: "Destroy this temple, and I will build it for you in three days." Had the Jews known a sign for him, they would not have said this, and had he manifested a miracle to them, he would have reminded them of it at that time.

And also in the Gospel that is in your hands: they came asking him for a sign, and he rebuffed them, and said: "This wicked, adulterous generation seeks a sign, but no sign shall be given to it."

And in it too: they used to say to him while he was on the cross, according to their supposition: "If you are the Messiah, then bring yourself down, and we will believe in you," seeking thereby a sign, but he did not do it.

So if you, assemblies of the Trinitarians, worshippers of the cross, disbelieve in the Qur'an, no sign or virtue is established for Jesus son of Mary. For your reports about him and the reports of the Jews are not to be relied upon, because of your extreme disagreement about his affair and your lack of certainty regarding all his matters.

Likewise, the Jews agreed that he never claimed any of the divinity you attribute to him.

Their ultimate aim was that he should claim it, so that their domination over him would be more complete. You have mentioned the reason why this report spread about him: when he passed away and his remembrance remained, their rabbis and scholars feared that the common people would turn to him, since he was upon a way that the hearts of those without ulterior motives would accept. So they vilified him with many matters and attributed to him the claim of divinity, to discourage people from his cause.

Furthermore, the Jews have so much disagreement about his affair that it shows they have no certainty about any of his reports. Some of them say he was a man from among them, and they know his father and mother, and they ascribe him to an adulteress. Far be it from him, and far be it from his mother, the truthful, pure, virgin who was never touched by any male. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded (﴿أنّى يُؤْفَكُونَ﴾, "how are they turned away?"). They name his father, for the adulteress, al-Bandira the Roman, and his mother Maryam the hairdresser. They allege that her husband, Yusuf ibn Yahuda, found al-Bandira with her on her bed, or sensed it, so he abandoned her and disowned her son.

Among the Jews, may Allah curse them, is one who turned away from this saying and said: his father was only Yusuf ibn Yahuda, who was the husband of Maryam. They mention that the reason the label of "bastard" (al-zanim) spread about him was this: one day he was with his teacher Yahshu' ibn Bardiya and the rest of the disciples, and they stopped at a place on a journey. A woman from his people came and began to exaggerate in honouring them. Yahshu' said: "How good is this woman?" meaning her deeds. Isa, according to their claim, said: "If only there were not a squint in her eye." Yahshu' cried out and said: "Mimzar" (its translation: "O bastard"), "do you commit adultery with a glance?" He became extremely angry, returned to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), prohibited his name, and cursed him for four hundred years. Then he joined some of the Roman commanders and entered them into the practice of medicine, and thereby he gained strength over the Jews, who at that time were under the protection of Caesar Batariyush. He began to oppose the ruling of the Torah (al-Tawrat), to add to it, and to turn away from some of it, until what happened to him happened.

Other groups of Jews, may Allah curse them, say otherwise. They say he used to play ball with the boys, and the ball stopped for them between a group of Jewish elders. The boys were too weak to retrieve it from among them, out of shame before their elders. Isa grew strong, stepped over their necks and took it. They said to him: "We do not think you are anything but a bastard."

Among the Jews' disagreements, may Allah curse them, about his affair is that they name his father, according to their claim, as the betrothed of Maryam: Yusuf ibn Yahuda the carpenter. Some of them say he was only Yusuf the blacksmith. The Christians claim she had a husband, and that her husband was Yusuf ibn Ya'qub. Some of them say Yusuf ibn Al.

They also differ about his ancestors and their number back to Ibrahim (peace be upon him): some reduce the number, and some increase it. This is what the Jews have, may Allah curse them, and they are your authorities in transmitting the crucifixion and its affair. Otherwise, it is known that none of the Christians was present at it. Rather, the Jews, may Allah curse them, were present, and they said: "We killed him and crucified him." It was they who said about him what we have related from them. If you believe them about the crucifixion, then believe them about everything else they have reported. If you disbelieve them regarding what they transmitted about him, then what justifies your believing them about the crucifixion and disbelieving them elsewhere? They did not crucify him; rather, Allah protected him, guarded him and preserved him, and he was more honoured with Allah and more esteemed in His sight than to be tested with what you say, may Allah fight you, and the Jews, may Allah curse them.

As for the account of what you yourselves hold, we know of no nation among the nations that is more divided over its object of worship, its prophet and its religion than you. If you asked a man, his wife, his daughter, his father and his mother about their religion, each one of them would answer you with an answer other than the answer of the others.

If ten of them gathered to discuss religion, they would disperse into eleven sects, despite the agreement of their well-known sects today on the belief in the Trinity, the worship of the cross, and that the Messiah, son of Maryam, is not a righteous servant, nor a prophet, nor a messenger, and that he is God in reality, and that he is the creator of the heavens, the earth, the angels and the prophets, and that he is the one who sent and manifested through them miracles and signs, and that the world has a God who is a father and begetter who has never ceased, and that his son descended from heaven and was embodied from the Holy Spirit and from Maryam, and that he and his human son became one God, one Messiah, one creator and one provider. Maryam conceived him and bore him; he was seized, crucified, tormented, died and was buried, rose after three days, ascended to heaven and sat at the right hand of his father.

They also said: "He whom Maryam bore, whom people witnessed and who was among them, is Allah, the Son of Allah, the Word of Allah."

So the Eternal, Pre-existent, Creator of the heavens and the earth is the one Maryam conceived, and he remained there for nine months. He is the one who was born, suckled, weaned, ate, drank, defecated, was seized, crucified, bound with ropes, and had his hands nailed.

Then they invented disputes. The Jacobites (al-Ya'qubiyya), may Allah fight them, who are the followers of Ya'qub al-Baradi'i, so named because his clothing was made of patches of animal harness (baradi' al-dawabb), which he patched together and wore, say: the Messiah is one nature (tabi'a) from two natures: one is the nature of humanity (al-nasut), and the other is the nature of divinity (al-lahut). These two natures combined and became one human being, one substance, one person. This one nature and one person is the Messiah. He is God entirely and man entirely, one person and one nature from two natures.

They also said: Maryam gave birth to God, and that God, glorified and exalted, was seized, crucified, nailed, died, was buried, and then lived after that.

Chapter: The Melkites (al-Maliikiyya), who are the Romans, named after the religion of the king and not after a man called Malikaya, who is said to be the founder of their doctrine, as some who lack knowledge of this claim. They say: the eternal Son, who is the Word, was embodied from Maryam with a complete embodiment like the bodies of all people. In that body he placed a complete soul with reason, knowledge and understanding, like the souls of all people. He became a human being by the body and the soul, which are of the substance of humans, and God by the substance of divinity like his father who has never ceased. He is a human by the substance of humanity like Ibrahim, Musa and Dawud. He is one person whose number did not increase, and the substance of divinity remained for him as it always was, and the substance of humanity which the son of Maryam wore became valid for him. He is one person whose number did not increase, and two natures, and each of the two natures has a complete will. He has a will of divinity like the Father, and a will of humanity like the will of Ibrahim and Dawud. They said: Maryam gave birth to the Messiah, a name that combines divinity and humanity. They said: the one who died is the one Maryam bore, and it is he upon whom the crucifixion, nailing, slapping and binding with ropes fell, while the divinity did not die, did not suffer and was not buried.

They said: He is God who stood by the substance of his divinity, and a man who stood by the substance of his humanity, and he has two wills: the will of divinity and the will of humanity. Thus they came with the same as the Jacobites, in that Maryam, according to them, gave birth to God, and they absolved God from death.

When you reflect upon their saying, you find it in reality to be the saying of the Jacobites, though they contradict themselves, and the Jacobites are more consistent in their unbelief, in word and in meaning.

As for the Nestorians (al-Nasturiyya), they went to the saying that the Messiah is two persons and two natures, with one will. When the nature of divinity came to exist in the humanity, they both had one will. Divinity does not accept increase or decrease, nor does it mix with anything, while humanity accepts increase and decrease. Thus the Messiah was God and man: he is God by the substance of divinity, which does not accept increase or decrease, and he is a man by the substance of humanity, which accepts increase and decrease. They said: Maryam gave birth to the Messiah in his humanity, and divinity never left him.

All these sects disdained that the Messiah should be a servant of Allah, while he himself did not disdain it, and he did not turn away from it. Rather, the highest of his ranks is the servitude of Allah. Muhammad and Ibrahim are better than him, and the highest of their ranks is perfecting the degrees of servitude to Allah, the Exalted. How fortunate is the one whom He was pleased to have as a servant. But the Trinitarians were not pleased with that.

The Arians (al-Aryusiyya) among them, who are the followers of Arius, said: the Messiah is a servant of Allah like the other prophets and messengers, a created, fashioned and owned being.

The Negus (al-Najashi) held this view.

When the Trinitarians overcame one of these, they killed him in the worst manner, and did to him what is done to whoever insults and reviles the Messiah with the greatest abuse.

Each of these three groups, their common folk, does not understand the statement of their elites in its true sense. Rather, they say: Allah passed over Maryam as a man passes over a woman, and impregnated her, and she bore Him a son. They do not know the nonsense their elites invented. They say: "What you are going on about, we believe in without needing to know the three regions, the two natures and the two wills, and that exaggeration and prolixity."

They openly declare that Maryam is the mother of God, and God is her father, and He is the Son. So this is husband, wife and child. And "they said: The Most Merciful has taken a son. You have indeed produced a monstrous thing, by which the heavens almost burst, the earth splits open and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son, when it is not fitting for the Most Merciful to take a son. There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant. He has enumerated them and counted them precisely, and each of them will come to Him alone on the Day of Resurrection." (Maryam 19:88–95)

These are the statements of the enemies of the Messiah: the Jews, the extremists among the Christians, and the Trinitarian worshippers of the cross. May Allah fight the two factions; how are they deluded.

Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ) with what removed the doubt about his affair, uncovered the confusion, and cleared the Messiah and his mother of what the Jews, may Allah curse them, had fabricated against them in slander, falsehood and lying, and of what the Trinitarian worshippers of the cross, who insulted him with the worst insult, had invented against him. May Allah fight them. The Lord of the worlds, the Creator of the Messiah and his mother, is exalted above what was fabricated against them. He placed his brother, the Messiah, in the station that Allah had placed him, which is the most noble of his stations. So he believed in him and affirmed him, and bore witness that he is the servant of Allah, His messenger and His spirit, and His word, which He cast to Maryam, the virgin, pure, truthful, the chief of the women of her time. He confirmed the Messiah's miracles and signs, and informed about his Lord, the Exalted, that whoever disbelieved in the Messiah will remain eternally in the Fire. He informed that his Lord, the Exalted, honoured His servant and messenger, purified and protected him, so that the brothers of apes, the people of wrath, would not obtain from him what the Christians claimed they had obtained from him. Rather, Allah raised him to Himself, supported and victorious, and his enemies did not harm him with a thorn, nor did their hands reach him with harm. Allah raised him to Himself and made him dwell in His heaven, and He will return him to the earth, where he will take vengeance through him upon the Antichrist (Masih al-Dalal) and his followers, then he will break the cross, kill the swine through him, exalt Islam through him, and support through him the religion of his brother, and the people most worthy of it is Muhammad (ﷺ).

When this statement about the Messiah is placed on one scale, and the statement of the Trinitarian worshippers of the cross on the other, it becomes clear to everyone who has even a little understanding how great the difference between them is, and that their difference is like the difference between it and the statement of those who earned anger (al-maghdub 'alayhim) regarding him. And success is from Allah.

Had it not been for Muhammad (ﷺ), we would not have known that the Messiah, son of Maryam, who is the messenger of Allah, His servant, His word and His spirit, exists at all. For this Messiah whom the Jews established is among the most evil of Allah's creation, and is not the Messiah of guidance.

The belief the Christians have affirmed is among the most manifest falsehoods. It cannot exist in reason or in natural disposition. Its existence is the most impossible of impossibilities. Had it been possible for it to exist, the proofs of reason would be nullified, and no one would have any trust in anything rational at all. The impossibility of its existence exceeds the impossibility of all impossible things. Had what they say been true, the world would perish, the heavens and the earth would be dissolved, the angels, the Throne and the Footstool would cease to exist, and there would be no resurrection, no gathering, no Paradise and no Fire.

It is no wonder that the nation of error, of whom God has testified that they are more astray than cattle, have unanimously agreed upon this. Every falsehood that exists in the world is attributed to some nation, and that nation is unanimous upon it. It has already been mentioned that the great nations, whose number none can count except God, Mighty and Majestic, agreed upon disbelief and error after witnessing the clear signs. So the worshippers of the Cross have a model in their brethren from among the people of polytheism and error.

(Section: Among the Glad Tidings of the Torah concerning the Messenger of God (ﷺ))

In the first book of the Torah (Tawrah): "God said to Abraham, 'I will make your son Ishmael into a great nation, for he is of your seed.'"

This is a glad tiding concerning the one from whose offspring a great nation would be made, and it is none other than Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah (ﷺ), who is of the very lineage of his son. He was made into a great nation. Whoever reflects upon this glad tiding will be certain that what is meant by it is the Messenger of God (ﷺ), because Ishmael's hand was never above the hand of Isaac, nor was Isaac's hand ever extended to him in submission. How could that be, when prophethood and kingship were among the children of Israel and Esau, and they were the two sons of Isaac? When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was sent, prophethood passed to the children of Ishmael, the nations submitted to him, the kings humbled themselves before him, and the succession to kingship was made to belong to his family until the end of time. Their hands came to be above the hands of all, and the hands of all were extended to them in submission.

Likewise, in the first book: "God, may He be exalted, said to Abraham, 'In this year a son will be born to you whose name is Isaac.' Abraham said, 'Would that Ishmael might live before you and glorify you.' God, may He be exalted, said: '[I have granted your request concerning Ishmael. I will bless him, make him grow, and magnify him greatly, greatly, by that in which I have granted your request. I will make him into a great and mighty nation, and I will give him a noble people.] No one came from the loins of Ishmael who was blessed and magnified, and upon whom these signs were fulfilled, other than the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his nation. They filled the horizons and multiplied in number beyond the seed of Isaac.'"

In the fifth book of the Torah it says: Moses said to the children of Israel, "Do not obey the soothsayers and the astrologers. The Lord, glorified and exalted, will raise up for you a prophet from among your brethren like me, so obey that prophet."

It is not permissible that this promised prophet be from among the children of Israel themselves, because it has already been stated that the brethren of a people are not the people themselves. As you say: "Bakr and Taghlib are the two sons of Wa'il." Then you say: "Taghlib is the brother of Bakr, and the children of Taghlib are the brothers of Bakr." If you said, "The brothers of the children of Bakr are the children of Bakr," it would be absurd. And if you said to a man, "Bring me a man from the brothers of the children of Bakr ibn Wa'il," it would be incumbent upon him to bring you a man from the children of Taghlib ibn Wa'il, not from among the children of Bakr.

In the Gospel (Injil) it is reported that the Messiah said to the disciples (Hawariyyun): "I am going away, and the Paraclete (al-Barqalit), the Spirit of truth, will come to you. He will not speak of his own accord; rather, he will say only what he is told. He will bear witness to me, and you will bear witness, because you have been with me from the beginning. Everything that God has prepared for you, he will inform you of."

In the Gospel of John: "The Paraclete will not come to you until I have gone. When he comes, he will convict the world concerning sin. He does not speak of his own accord, but he will speak to you of what he hears, will guide you with truth, and will inform you of events and of the unseen."

In another place: "I will ask my Father to send you another Paraclete who will be the teacher of eternity, and he will teach you everything."

In another place: "The Son of Man is departing, and the Paraclete will come after him and bring you the secrets, and will explain to you everything. He will bear witness to me as I have borne witness to him. I bring you parables, and he will bring you the interpretation."

Abu Muhammad ibn Qutayba said: These statements, despite their variation, are close in meaning. They differ because those who transmitted them from the Messiah (ﷺ) in the Gospel were the disciples after him, and the word Paraclete (al-Barqalit) in their language is among the words of praise, whether it means Ahmad, or Muhammad, or Mahmud, or Hamid, or the like... In the Ethiopian Gospel it is Barafqitis.

In another place: "If you love me, keep my commandments, and I will ask the Father to give you another Paraclete who will remain with you forever, and who will speak by the Spirit of truth, which the world could not receive, because they do not know it. I will not leave you orphans, for I will come to you soon."

In another place: "Whoever loves me by keeping my word will be loved by my Father, and to him he will come and make his dwelling with him. I have told you this because I am not going to remain with you. The Paraclete is the Spirit of truth whom my Father will send, and he will teach you everything and remind you of all that I have said to you. I leave you my peace. Do not let your hearts be troubled, and do not be afraid, for I am going away and I will return to you. If you loved me, you would rejoice that I am going to my Father. If my word abides in you, you will have all that you desire."

In another place: "When the Paraclete whom my Father sends, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from my Father, comes, he will bear witness to me that I have said this, so that you may believe in him and not doubt concerning him."

In another place: "I have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now. But when the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth, for he does not speak from himself, but speaks what he hears, and will tell you all that is to come and make known to you all that belongs to the Father." John said: The Messiah said, "The ruler of this world is coming, and he has nothing in me." Matthew said: The Messiah said, "Have they not read that the stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone? This is from God, and it is marvelous in our eyes. Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken from you and given to a nation that will produce its fruit. Whoever falls upon this stone will be broken, and whoever it falls upon will be crushed."

The Paraclete has been disputed in their language, meaning Hebrew, and they have mentioned views concerning it that return to three aspects.

The first: that it means "the one who praises," and praise, as previously mentioned. A group preferred this view and said: "What is established by proof in their language is that it means praise. The evidence for this is in the words of Joshua (Yushaʿ): 'Whoever does a good deed will have a good Faraqlit,' i.e., a good praise."

The second view, which most Christians hold, is that it means "the Savior (al-Mukhallis)." They call the Messiah himself "the Savior," and this is a Syriac word meaning "the Savior." They said: in Syriac it is Farus, so it became "Faraq," and they said "lit" is an added element, meaning as in the Arabs' saying: "a man himself, a stone itself, a horse itself." They said: thus the meaning of "lit" in Syriac is likewise.

The third view: another group of Christians said its meaning in Syriac is "the Comforter (al-Muʿazzi)." They said it is likewise in the Greek tongue. This view is objected to on the basis that the Messiah's language was not Syriac nor Greek, but Hebrew. This is answered by saying that he spoke in Hebrew, and the Gospel was revealed in the Hebrew language, and it was translated into Syriac, Latin, Greek and others.

Most Christians hold that it means "the Savior," and the Messiah himself they call "the Savior." In the Gospel that is in their hands, it is said that he said: "I came only to save the world."

The Christians say in their prayer: "You have been born for us as a Savior."

Since the Christians could not deny these texts, they distorted them in various kinds of distortion. Some of them said: it is a spirit that descended upon the disciples. Some said: it is fiery tongues that descended from heaven upon the followers, so they performed signs and wonders through them. Some claim that it is the Messiah himself, because he came forty days after the Crucifixion and because he rose from his grave. Some said: we do not know what is meant by this Paraclete, and its meaning is not verified for us.

Whoever considers the words of the Gospel and its context knows that its interpretation as the Spirit is false, and more false than it is its interpretation as the fiery tongues, and more false than both of them is its interpretation as the Messiah. For the Holy Spirit has continually descended upon the prophets and the righteous before the Messiah and after him, and it is not described with these attributes. God, the Exalted, has said: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in God and the Last Day loving those who oppose God and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers or their kindred. Those—He has written faith into their hearts and strengthened them with a spirit from Himself.﴾

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to Hassan ibn Thabit, may God be pleased with him, when he was satirizing the polytheists: "O God, support him with the Holy Spirit." And he said: "The Holy Spirit is with you as long as you defend His Prophet."

Since this is so, and no one has named this Spirit "Faraqlit," it is known that the Paraclete is something other than this. Moreover, such a Spirit has always been the support of the prophets and the righteous, while what the Messiah announced and promised is a great matter that will come after him, greater than this. For he described the Paraclete with attributes that do not suit this Spirit, but suit a man who will come after him as his counterpart. He said: "If you love me, keep my commandments, and I will ask the Father to give you another Faraqlit who will remain with you forever." His saying "another Faraqlit" indicates that he is a second to a first who was before him, and that he was not with them during the life of the Messiah, but would come after his departure and his passing. Moreover, he said: "He will remain with you forever," and this applies only to what endures and remains with them until the end of time. It is known that he did not intend the continuance of his own person, so it is understood that he meant the continuance of his law and command. The first Paraclete did not have his law and religion remain with them forever. This shows that the second is the bearer of a law that will not be abrogated but will remain forever, unlike the first. This applies only to Muhammad (ﷺ).

Furthermore, he informed that this Paraclete of whom he spoke bears witness to him, teaches them everything, reminds them of all that he said, and convicts the world of its sin.

He said: "The Faraqlit whom my Father sends will teach you everything and remind you of all that I have told you."

He said: "When the Faraqlit whom my Father sends comes, he will bear witness for me that I said this, so that you may believe in him and not doubt concerning him."

He said: "It is good for you that I go to my Father. If I do not go, the Faraqlit will not come to you. But when I depart, I will send him to you. He will convict the world of sin. I have many things to say, but you cannot bear them now.
