But when the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth, for he does not speak from himself, but speaks what he hears, and will tell you of all that is to come and make known to you all that belongs to the Father."

So these attributes and descriptions that they received from the Messiah do not apply to some inward matter that exists in the heart of certain people, which no one sees and whose speech no one hears. Rather, they apply to one whom people see and whose speech they hear: he bears witness to the Messiah, teaches them everything, reminds them of all that the Messiah said to them, reproves the world concerning sin, guides people to all the truth, does not speak from his own self but speaks only what he hears, and informs them of all that is to come, and makes known to them all that belongs to the Lord of the worlds. This cannot be an angel whom no one sees, nor can it be guidance and knowledge in the hearts of certain people. It can only be a man of great station who addresses people with what the Messiah told them, and this can only be a human messenger, indeed one greater than the Messiah. For the Messiah stated that he (the one to come) is able to do what the Messiah cannot do, knows what the Messiah does not know, and informs of all that is to come and of what is due to the Lord, when he said: "Indeed I have much to say which I wish to tell you, but you cannot bear it. But when the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth, for he does not speak from himself, but speaks what he hears, and he will tell you what is to come, and make known to you all that belongs to the Father."

No sensible person doubts that these attributes apply only to Muhammad (ﷺ). This is because informing about Allah, the Exalted, concerning what He is characterized by of attributes, and about His angels, His kingdom, and what He has prepared in Paradise for His friends and in Hell for His enemies, is a matter that most people's minds cannot bear to know in detail.

ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Speak to people in terms of what they know, and leave aside what they deny. Do you want Allah and His Messenger to be denied?"

Ibn Masʿūd said: "No man speaks to a people with a saying that their minds cannot reach without it becoming a trial for some of them."

A man asked Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him, about the words of the Exalted: {Allah is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them; the command descends among them…}. He said: "What assures you that if I informed you of it you would not disbelieve? … meaning, if I informed you of its explanation you would disbelieve in it, and your disbelief in it is your denial of it."

So the Messiah said to them: "Indeed I have much to say to you which I wish to say, but you cannot bear it," and he is the truthful one whose truthfulness is affirmed in this matter.

For this reason, there is nothing in the Gospel of the attributes of Allah, the Exalted, and the attributes of His kingdom and of the Last Day except general matters. Likewise, the Torah contains nothing of mention of the Last Day except general matters, even though Moses, peace be upon him, had prepared the way for the affair of the Messiah. Yet, despite this, the Messiah said to them: "Indeed I have much to say to you which I wish to say, but you cannot bear it." Then he said: "But when the Spirit of truth comes, he is the one who will guide you to the truth, and will inform you of all that is to come, and of all that belongs to the Lord."

This indicates that the Paraclete is the one who does this, not the Messiah, and so it was. Muhammad (ﷺ) guided people to all the truth until Allah perfected the religion through him and completed His blessing through him. For this reason he was the Seal of the Prophets, for nothing remains that could be brought other than by him. Muhammad (ﷺ) informed of everything to come of the signs of the Hour, the Resurrection, the Reckoning, the Bridge, the weighing of deeds, Paradise and its kinds of bliss, and Hell and its kinds of punishment. For this reason, the Qur'an contains a detailed account of the matter of the Hereafter and the mention of Paradise and Hell. He brings many matters that are not found in the Torah and the Gospel, and this confirms the Messiah's statement, peace be upon him, that he would be informed of all that is to come. This implies the truthfulness of both the Messiah and Muhammad (ﷺ).

This is the meaning of the words of the Exalted: {Indeed, when it was said to them, "There is no deity except Allah," they were arrogant and said, "Shall we leave our gods for a mad poet?" Rather, he has brought the truth and confirmed the messengers} (37:35–37). That is, his coming is a confirmation of the messengers before him, for they informed of his coming and he came as they had informed, so his coming includes confirmation of them. Then he himself testified to their truthfulness and confirmed them by his words and his coming.

Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent by Allah in the time just before the Hour, as he said: "I and the Hour have been sent like these two," and he pointed with his two fingers, the index and the middle finger. When he mentioned the Hour, his voice would rise, his face would redden, and his anger would intensify, and he would say: "I am the plain warner."

He informed of matters yet to come that no prophet had informed of, just as the Messiah described him when he said: "He will tell you all that is to come." Such a thing is not found at all concerning any prophet before Muhammad (ﷺ), let alone found in a book revealed upon the heart of some of the disciples. Also, he said: "And he will make known to you all that belongs to the Lord."

He made clear that he makes known to people all that belongs to Allah, and this encompasses what belongs to Allah of names and attributes, what is due to Him, and what must be believed in of Him, His angels, His books, and His messengers, so that what he brings comprises all that the Lord, glorified and exalted, deserves. No one other than Muhammad (ﷺ) brought this, for it includes what he brought of the Book and the Wisdom.

All of this, and also, the Messiah said: "When the Paraclete comes, whom my Father will send, he will bear witness to me that I told you this, so that when it happens you will believe in him."

So he informed that he would bear witness to him, and this is the description of a prophet whom the Messiah announced, who bears witness to the Messiah, as the Exalted said: {And when Jesus, son of Mary, said, "O Children of Israel, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you, confirming what is before me of the Torah and giving glad tidings of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad"} (61:6).

He also informed that he would reprove the world concerning sin, and this cannot be understood as a meaning existing in the hearts of the disciples, for they believed in him and bore witness to him before his departure. How then could he say: "When he comes, he will bear witness to me, and will instruct them to believe in him"? Do you think the disciples were not believers in the Messiah? This is among the greatest ignorance and error of the Christians.

Also, no one has been found who reproved the entire world concerning sin except Muhammad (ﷺ), for he warned all the world of all kinds of people and reproved them for sin, of disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience. He did not limit himself to mere command and prohibition, but reproved them, frightened them, and threatened them.

Also, he informed that he does not speak from his own self but speaks only what he hears. This is an informing that everything he says is revelation that he hears; it is not something he learned from people or came to know by deduction, and this is a distinction peculiar to Muhammad (ﷺ).

As for the Messiah, he had knowledge of what Moses brought before him, which he shared with the People of the Book, having received it from those before him; then there came to him a special revelation from Allah beyond what he had. The Exalted said: {And He will teach him the Book and the Wisdom, and the Torah and the Gospel} (3:48). So He, glorified and exalted, informed that He teaches him the Torah that the Children of Israel learned, and adds to him the teaching of the Gospel, which was specific to him, and the Book, which is writing. But Muhammad (ﷺ) had not learned anything at all before the revelation, as the Exalted said: {And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor faith} (42:52).

And the Exalted said: {We relate to you the best of stories by what We have revealed to you of this Qur'an, though before it you were certainly among the unaware} (12:3). So he (ﷺ) did not speak from his own self; rather his speech was only by revelation, as the Exalted said: {Nor does he speak from desire. It is not but revelation that is revealed} (53:3–4). This agrees with the Messiah's saying that he does not speak from his own self but speaks only what is revealed to him.

Allah, the Exalted, commanded him to convey what was sent down to him, and guaranteed him protection in conveying His messages. Therefore he guided people to all the truth, and he conveyed to people what no other prophet had conveyed, out of fear that his people would kill him. The Messiah had informed that he did not mention to them all that he had, and that they could not bear it, and they themselves acknowledge that he feared them when he told them the realities of matters. But Muhammad (ﷺ), whom Allah, glorified and exalted, supported with a support He gave to no one else, protected him from people so that he feared nothing he said, and gave him of eloquence and knowledge what He did not give to anyone else.

So the Book with which he was sent contains a clarification of the realities of the Unseen that is not in the book of anyone else, and He strengthened his community with a strengthening by which they were able to bear what he conveyed to them. So they were not like the People of the Torah, who were charged with the Torah and then did not bear it, nor like the People of the Gospel, to whom the Messiah said: "Indeed I have much to say to you which I wish to say, but you cannot bear it."

There is no doubt that the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) is more complete in intellect, greater in faith, and fuller in affirmation and struggle. For this reason their knowledge and their inward deeds and faith are greater, and the bodily acts of worship of others are greater.

Also, he informed concerning the Paraclete that he bears witness to him, and that he teaches them everything, and that he reminds them of all that the Messiah said. It is known that this cannot happen unless he bore witness to him with a testimony that common people hear; it cannot be in the heart of a small group. No one bore witness to the Messiah with a testimony that the common people heard except Muhammad (ﷺ), for he made the affair of the Messiah manifest and bore witness to him with the truth, until the common people of the earth heard his testimony for him, and they knew that he affirmed the Messiah and cleared him of what the Jews said against him of falsehood and of what the Christians exaggerated concerning him.

So he is the one who bore witness to him with the truth. For this reason, when the Negus heard from the Companions what Muhammad (ﷺ) testified about the Messiah, he said to them: "Jesus did not exceed what you have said by this stick."

And Allah made the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) witnesses over mankind, bearing witness against them with what they know of the truth, since they are a middle, just community that does not bear witness to falsehood, for a witness must be just, unlike one who acts unjustly in his testimony, adding to the truth or diminishing from it, like the testimony of the Jews and the Christians concerning the Messiah.

Also, if the meaning of Paraclete is "the one who praises," or "the much-praising," or "the praised," or "praise," then this is a description manifestly applicable to Muhammad (ﷺ), for he and his community are the praisers who praise Allah in every state. He is the bearer of the banner of praise, praise is the key to his sermon and the key to his prayer. And since he was much-praising, he was named with a name matching his description, Muhammad, on the pattern of "mukarram," "muqaddas," and "muʿaẓẓam," and he is the one who praises more than others praise, and deserves that. So since he was much-praising of Allah, he was Muhammad. And in the poetry of Ḥassān:

Radiant, upon him is the seal of prophethood, from Allah, blessed, shining and bearing witness.
Allah joined the name of the Prophet to His own name: when the muezzin says in the five prayers, "I bear witness…"
And He cleaved for him a name from His own name to honour him: the Lord of the Throne is Maḥmūd, and this is Muḥammad.

As for Aḥmad, it is the comparative form (ʿafʿal al-tafḍīl), meaning he is more praiseworthy than others, that is, more deserving of being praised more than others. It is said: "This is more praiseworthy than that," meaning this is more deserving of being praised than that, so there is in it a preference over others in being praised. Thus the word Muḥammad implies an increase in quantity, and the word Aḥmad implies an increase in quality.

Some people say its meaning is that he praises Allah more than others do, and on this view it has the meaning of the praiser and the much-praiser, while on the first view it has the meaning of the praised.

And if Paraclete means praise, then it is a noun used as a name for the sake of intensification in the abundance of praise, as one says "a man of justice" (ʿadl), "of contentment" (riḍan), and similar. By this the secret of what the Qur'an reports of the Messiah's words is made clear: {and giving glad tidings of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Aḥmad} (61:6).

For this is the meaning of Paraclete, as has already been stated.

In the Torah there is a text which, translated into Arabic, reads: "As for Ishmael, I have heard your prayer. I have blessed him, made him fruitful, and I will multiply him greatly through *Mu'ad Mu'ad*." This word, *Mu'ad Mu'ad*, is on the pattern of *Umar*, and the scholars of the People of the Book have differed about it. One group says its meaning is "very, very" (*jiddan jiddan*), that is, "exceedingly much." If this is its meaning, it is a good tidings of one whose greatness from his Prophet is very, very great, and it is known that no one was magnified from his Prophet more than Muhammad (ﷺ).

Another group said: rather, it is the explicit name of Muhammad. They said: what indicates this is that the words of Hebrew are close to the words of Arabic, as it is the closest of languages to Arabic. They say *Shma'il* for Ishmael, *Shim'atkha* for "I heard you," *Anu* for "I" (*Ana*), *Shatha* for "sanctified you" (*qaddasaka*), *Atta* for "you" (*anta*), and *Yisra'il* for Israel. Consider His saying in the Torah: "*Qadesh li kol bekhor rekhem bevnei Yisra'el ba-adam uve-behemah li*."

Its meaning: "Consecrate to Me every firstborn or womb-opener among the children of Israel, from human to animal, to Me." Consider also His saying: "*Navi akim lahem mi-tokh akhihem kamokha lo tishma'un*," whose meaning is: "I will raise up for them a prophet from among their brothers, like you, to whom you shall listen." Likewise His saying: "*Atem 'overim be-gevul akhikhem benei Esau*," meaning: "You are passing through the borders of your brothers, the children of Esau." Examples of this are more numerous than can be mentioned.

When you take the word *Mu'ad Mu'ad*, you find it closest to the word Muhammad. If you wish to verify this, then match the words of Hebrew with Arabic. For this reason they say *Esba'u Elohim*, meaning "the finger of God," by which He wrote the Torah for him.

What indicates this is the particle "*ba*" (with) in His saying: "with *Mu'ad Mu'ad*." One does not say "I magnify him with *jiddan jiddan*," unlike "I magnify him with Muhammad (ﷺ)." Likewise, he was magnified through him and his honour increased by his honour. Rather, the magnifying of him through Muhammad (ﷺ), his son, surpasses the magnifying of every father for his son of great rank. So God, glorified and exalted, multiplied him through Muhammad (ﷺ).

Under both interpretations, the text is among the clearest of the good tidings concerning him. As for this interpretation, it is evident, very, very evident. As for the first interpretation, He multiplied Ishmael and magnified him above Isaac very, very much through his son Muhammad (ﷺ).

If you match the meaning of *Paraclete* with the meaning of *Mu'ad Mu'ad*, and the meaning of Muhammad and Ahmad, and you consider the qualities of praise (*hamd*) that are in him, and his naming his community "the praisers" (*al-hamidun*), and the opening of his Book with praise, and the opening of the prayer with praise, and the abundance of the qualities of praise that are in him, in his community, in his religion, and in his Book; and you know what he delivered the world from of the kinds of polytheism, disbelief, sins and innovations, and speaking about God without knowledge; and what God strengthened the truth and its people with through him, and what He suppressed falsehood and its party by means of him; you will be certain that he is the *Farqalit* (Paraclete) in all respects.

Who is this, who is the Spirit of Truth, who speaks only what is revealed to him?! And who is the one who succeeds the Messiah, and the witness to what he brought, and the confirmer of him by his coming?! And who is the one who informed us of events and future times, such as the emergence of the Dajjal, the appearance of the Beast, the rising of the sun from its west, the emergence of Gog and Magog, the descent of the Messiah son of Mary, the appearance of the Fire that gathers people, and a multiplication of many times over of the unseen matters that come before the Day of Resurrection, and the unseen matters that occur on the Day of Resurrection: the Bridge, the Balance, the Reckoning, the taking of the books in the right hand and the left, and the details of what is in Paradise and Hell, which were not mentioned in the Torah or the Gospel? Other than Muhammad (ﷺ), who else? And who else rebuked the world for its sins? And who else informed the community of what is fitting for God in the truest sense of informing? And who else speaks in this domain with what most of the world could not bear to accept, to the extent that many minds that believed in him and affirmed him were unable to grasp it, so they subjected it to various kinds of distortion and interpretation because their minds were incapable of bearing it, just as his brother the Messiah said, peace and blessings of God be upon them both?

And who else was sent to all creation, in word, deed and belief, in knowledge of God, His names, attributes, rulings, actions, decree and destiny, other than him (ﷺ)?! And who is the *Arkun al-'Alam* (the Ruler/Chief of the world) who came after the Messiah, other than him? *Arkun al-'Alam* is the greatest of the world and its chief. Consider the Messiah's saying in this tidings, which they do not deny: that the Arkun of the world will come, and "I have no authority over it." How can this be, when it bears witness to the prophethood of the Messiah and the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) together? For when he came, the authority became his, not the Messiah's. Therefore it became obligatory upon the whole world to obey him and submit to his command, and authority truly became his. Nothing remains in the hands of the Christians but a religion whose falsehood is many times over its truth, and its truth has been abrogated (*mansukh*) by what God sent Muhammad (ﷺ) with. Thus the saying of the Messiah matched the saying of his brother Muhammad (ﷺ): "The son of Mary will descend among you as a just judge and a equitable leader, and he will judge by the Book of your Lord," and his saying in another wording: "He will lead you by the Book of your Lord." Thus the words of the two noble Messengers agree, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon them both: the first gave good tidings of the second, and the second confirmed the first.

Consider his saying in the other tidings: "Have you not read: the stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone?" How you find it matching the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "My parable and the parable of the prophets before me is like a man who built a house, completed and perfected it, except for the place of one brick. The people went around it, marvelling at it, and said: 'Why was that brick not placed?' So I was that brick."

Consider the Messiah's saying in this tidings: "Indeed, that is wondrous in our eyes." Consider also his saying in it: "The kingdom of God will be taken from you and given to another nation." How you find it matching His saying, exalted is He: "And We have certainly written in the Psalms, after the Reminder, that the earth shall be inherited by My righteous servants."

And His saying, exalted is He: "God has promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors in the earth, as He made successors those before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and that He will surely change their state after their fear into security. They shall worship Me, not associating anything with Me. And whoever disbelieves after that, those are the defiantly disobedient."

Consider his saying about the promised Paraclete: "He will disclose to you the secrets and explain to you everything. For I come to you with parables, but he comes to you with interpretation." How you find it corresponding to reality in every respect, in accordance with His saying, exalted is He: "And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things," and His saying, exalted is He: "It is not a narration invented, but a confirmation of what is before it and a detailed explanation of all things, and a guidance and mercy for a people who believe."

When you consider the Torah, the Gospel and the (other) books, and consider the Qur'an, you find it as the elaboration of their summaries, the interpretation of their parables, and the explanation of their symbols. This is the reality of the Messiah's saying: "I come to you with parables, and he comes to you with interpretation, and he explains to you everything."

When you consider his saying: "And everything God has prepared for you, he will inform you of it," and the details of what he informed of concerning Paradise and Hell, reward and punishment, you will be certain of the truthfulness of the two noble Messengers, and of the agreement of the detailed report from Muhammad (ﷺ) with the summarized report from his brother the Messiah, peace be upon him. Consider his saying about the Paraclete: "He will bear witness to me as I bore witness to him." How you find it applying precisely to Muhammad son of 'Abdullah, and how you find him bearing witness to the truthfulness of the two Messengers, and how you find him explicit about a man who comes after the Messiah, bearing witness for him that he is the servant and messenger of God, as the Messiah bore witness for him?!

The Messiah proclaimed the prophethood of Muhammad, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon them both, with a call that no prophet before him had proclaimed. He announced with the glorifying of his Lord: "How could He have a consort or a son?" Then he raised his voice with the testimony that there is no god but God alone, without partner, one God, one, single, eternal, who does not beget nor is begotten, and there is none comparable to Him. Then he proclaimed the testimony that Muhammad is His servant and messenger, the witness to his prophethood, supported by the Spirit of Truth, who does not speak from his own desire but speaks only what is revealed to him and teaches them everything and informs them of what God has prepared for them. Then he raised his voice with "Come to success" by following him, believing in him and affirming him, and that there is nothing of the command for him. He concluded the call by saying that the kingdom of God will be taken from those who denied him and given to his followers and believers in him. So whoever perished, perished with clear proof, and whoever lived, lived with clear proof. The followers of the Messiah truly responded to this call, while the disbelievers and deniers refused it. Thus God, exalted is He, said: "I will take you and raise you to Me and purify you from those who disbelieve, and I will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ."

This is a tidings that the Muslims will continue to be above the Christians until the Day of Resurrection, for the Muslims are truly the followers of the Messengers, and the followers of all the prophets, not their enemies. Their enemies are the worshippers of the Cross, who were content for him to be a god crucified, slain, and killed, and were not content for him to be a prophet, a servant of God, honoured by Him and brought near to Him. These are truly his enemies, and the Muslims are truly his followers.

The point is that the tidings of the Messiah concerning the Prophet (ﷺ) surpasses every tidings, since he was the closest of the prophets to him and the most entitled to him, and there is no prophet between them who was a sent messenger bearing a law and a book.

(Section):
Consider the Messiah's saying: "The Arkun of the world will come," and the Arkun of the world is its lord and greatest. Who ruled the world and was obeyed by the world after the Messiah, other than the Prophet, peace be upon him?!

Consider the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ), when he was asked: "What was the beginning of your affair?" He said: "I am the answer to the prayer of my father Abraham, and the glad tidings of Jesus."

Match this with the tidings which the Messiah mentioned: who ruled the world outwardly and inwardly, to whom hearts and bodies submitted, who was obeyed in secret and openly, in his life and after his death, in all ages and in the best regions and cities; whose call travelled like the sun across the lands, whose religion reached as far as the night and day reach; before whose coming nations prostrated upon their chins, through whom the worship of idols was nullified, through whom the call of the Most Merciful was established, through whom the call of Satan was crushed, who humiliated the disbelievers and deniers and honoured the believers, who came with the truth and confirmed the Messengers, until he proclaimed the Oneness (of God) before the eyes of the witnesses, and worshipped God alone without partner in every settled place and desert; with whom the earth was filled with praising, glorifying and magnifying God, and was clothed, after oppression and darkness, with justice and light?

(Section)
Match the saying of the Messiah, "The Arkun of the world will come to you," with the saying of his brother Muhammad (ﷺ): "I am the master of the children of Adam, and I say this without boasting. Adam and all after him are under my banner. I am the orator of the prophets when they come as a delegation, their leader when they assemble, and their bearer of glad tidings when they despair. The banner of praise is in my hand, and I am the most honoured of the children of Adam before my Lord."

(Section):
In the saying of the Messiah in this tidings, "I have no authority over it," there is an indication of the Oneness (of God) and that the whole matter belongs to God. So this tidings included the two foundations of the religion: the affirmation of Oneness and the affirmation of prophethood.

What the Messiah said corresponds to what his brother Muhammad son of 'Abdullah brought from his Lord, in His saying: "You have no authority in the matter at all."

Whoever considers the state of the two noble Messengers and their call finds them in complete agreement and correspondence, step for step, and it is impossible ever to believe in one of them while denying the other. For whoever denies Muhammad (ﷺ) is far more a denier of the Messiah, who is the Messiah son of Mary, the servant and messenger of God. And if he believes in a Messiah who has no reality and no existence, then he is in the greatest falsehood.

John said in the book of the Acts of the Apostles, which they call Afrakis: "My beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God, for many false prophets have gone out into the world. Every spirit that confesses that Yasu' al-Masih (Jesus the Messiah) has come in the flesh is from God, and every spirit that does not confess that the Messiah has come in the flesh is not from God, but is from the antichrist, the false Messiah, who is now in the world."

So the Muslims believe in the true Messiah, who came from God with guidance and the religion of truth. He is the servant of God and His messenger, and His word which He cast to Maryam (Mary) the virgin, the pure. The Christians believe only in a Messiah who called people to worship himself and his mother, and who said that he is the third of three, and that he is God or the Son of God. This is the brother of the false Messiah, if he had any existence.

The false Messiah claims that he is God, and the Christians in reality are followers of this false Messiah, just as the Jews await his coming. They claim that they await the Prophet about whom they were given good news, but after his coming Satan substituted for their belief in him the waiting for the false Messiah (al-Masih al-Dajjal). Thus everyone who turns away from the truth is compensated with falsehood.

The root of this is that when Iblis turned away from prostrating to Adam out of arrogance, refusing to submit to him, he was compensated for that with the humiliation of being led by every wicked and criminal among his offspring. Neither with that pride nor with this trade. When the Christians disdained that the Messiah should be a servant of God, they were compensated for this disdain by agreeing to make him a target for the Jews, their crucifixion whom they mocked and ridiculed. Then they placed on him a crown of thorns instead of the crown of kingship, and led him with a rope to the cross, clapping around him and dancing. Neither with that disdain of servitude to God, nor with this attribution to him of the greatest humiliation, subjugation and oppression.

Likewise, they disdained that a monk or a priest should have a wife or a child, yet they attributed to Allah, Lord of the worlds, a son and a wife. Likewise, they disdained worshipping God alone, with no partner, and obeying His servant and messenger, yet they were content with worshipping the cross and images made by hands on the walls, and with obeying everyone who forbids for them what he wills, permits for them what he wills, and legislates for them in religion what he wills, from his own accord.

A parallel to this compensation is that the Jahmiyyah (a sect that denies God's attributes) disdained that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, should be above His heavens on His Throne, separate from His creation, so that, in their claim, He would not be confined to a specific direction. Then they said: "He is in every place in His essence." So they confined Him to wells, prisons, filth and latrines, and compensated for His glorious Throne with these places. So let the intelligent person reflect on how Satan plays with the minds of these people, laughs at them, and mocks them.

(Section):
The statement of the Messiah: "When I depart, I will send him to you" means that I will send him by my supplication and my request that he send him, just as a seeker asks the ruler to send a messenger, or appoint a deputy, or give someone something, and the ruler says: "I sent this one, appointed him and gave him," meaning that he was the cause of that. When Allah, glorified and exalted is He, decrees that a thing should occur, He ordains for it causes by which it occurs, and among those causes is the supplication of some of His servants that He do that. In this there is a blessing, the answering of his supplication, added to His blessing of bringing into existence what He decreed. Muhammad (ﷺ) was asked for by the Friend (Khalil, Ibrahim), upon whom be prayers and peace, his father, when he said: ﴿Our Lord, raise among them a messenger from among them, who will recite to them Your verses, and teach them the Book and wisdom, and purify them. Indeed, You are the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾

Even though Allah, glorified and exalted is He, had decreed his sending and announced his name before that, as it was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, when did you become a prophet?" He said: "Adam was between the spirit and the body," and he said: "Indeed I am written with Allah as the Seal of the Prophets, while Adam was still lying in his clay."

This is like how Allah, glorified and exalted is He, decreed His victory on the day of Badr, and among the causes of that was his seeking help from his Lord, his supplication and his imploring for victory. Likewise, what He decrees of sending down rain, He may make it occur because of the imploring, supplication and humble entreaty of His servants to Him. Likewise, what He decrees of forgiveness, mercy, guidance and victory, He may cause supplications by which it is attained, by the one who receives it or by others. So there is nothing impossible in the Messiah having asked his Lord, after his ascension and rising to heaven, to send his brother Muhammad (ﷺ) to the world, and that this be among the causes of his sending, in addition to the supplication of his father Ibrahim. But Ibrahim asked his Lord to send him in this world, so Allah, glorified and exalted is He, mentioned that. As for the Messiah, he asked for it only after his lifting and ascension to heaven, as he had promised before his lifting.

(Section):
Reflect on the words of the Messiah: "I will not leave you as orphans; I will come to you soon," how exactly it corresponds to the words of his brother Muhammad ibn Abdullah, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them both: "The son of Maryam will descend among you as a just judge and a equitable leader, and he will kill the swine, break the cross, and abolish the jizya (poll tax), and he will instruct his community that whoever meets him among them should convey his greetings."

And in another hadith: "How can a nation perish when I am at its beginning and Isa (Jesus) is at its end?!"

(Section):
The text of the Torah has already been cited: "God shone forth from Mount Sinai, and rose from Se'ir, and appeared from the mountains of Paran."

The scholars of Islam said, and this is the wording of Abu Muhammad ibn Qutaybah: "There is no obscurity or ambiguity in this to whoever reflects upon it. Because the coming, i.e., the coming of God from Mount Sinai, is His sending down of the Torah upon Musa (Moses) from Mount Sinai, as it is according to the People of the Book and according to us. Likewise, His shining forth from Se'ir must be His sending down of the Gospel upon the Messiah. The Messiah was from Se'ir, the land of Khalil (Ibrahim), in a village called Nasirah, and by its name those who followed him were called Nasara (Christians). And just as His shining forth from Se'ir was with the Messiah, so His appearing from the mountains of Paran is His sending down of the Qur'an upon Muhammad (ﷺ). The mountains of Paran are the mountains of Makkah." He said: "There is no dispute between the Muslims and the People of the Book that Paran is Makkah. If they claim that it is other than Makkah, and this denial is no surprise given their distortion and falsehood, we say: Is it not in the Torah that Ibrahim settled Hajar and Isma'il in Paran?! We say to them: Show us the place from which Allah appeared, whose name is Paran, and the prophet upon whom He sent down a book after the Messiah."

Is not "appeared" (istu'lina) and "became manifest" (ʿalana) with one meaning, namely appeared and was revealed? So do you know of a religion that appeared as Islam appeared and spread in the east and west of the earth? If so, show it to us."

The scholars of Islam said: "Se'ir is a mountain range in Syria. From it the prophethood of the Messiah appeared, beside the village of Bayt Lahm (Bethlehem), the village in which the Messiah was born, and today it is called Se'ir."

In the Torah it is said that the offspring of Esau were inhabitants of Se'ir, and Allah commanded Musa not to harm them.

Shaykh al-Islam said, meaning Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him: "According to this, He has mentioned the three mountains, and Hira, which is not around Makkah, is higher than it, and in it the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began receiving revelation, and around it are many mountains. And that place is called Paran to this day, and the wilderness between Makkah and Mount Sinai is called the Wilderness of Paran. No one can claim that after the Messiah a book was sent down in any of those places, nor that a prophet was sent. So it is known that the intended meaning of His appearing from the mountains of Paran is nothing but the sending of Muhammad (ﷺ). He, glorified is He, mentioned this in the Torah in chronological order, so He mentioned the sending down of the Torah, then the Gospel, then the Qur'an. These books are the light of God, the Exalted, and His guidance. He said of the first: 'came,' of the second: 'shone forth,' and of the third: 'appeared.' The coming of the Torah was like the break of dawn, the descent of the Gospel was like the rising of the sun, and the descent of the Qur'an was like the sun shining in the sky. For this reason He said: 'and appeared from the mountains of Paran,' for Muhammad (ﷺ) made the light and guidance of God manifest in the east and west of the earth more greatly than was manifested by the two earlier books, just as the light of the sun shines in the east and west of the earth when it rises and reaches the middle of the sky. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, called him a 'radiant lamp' (siraj munir), and called the sun a 'blazing lamp' (siraj wahhaj). People need the radiant lamp more than they need the blazing lamp, for they need the latter at one time and not another, whereas they need the radiant lamp at all times, in every place, by night and by day, in private and in public."

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has mentioned these three places in His saying: ﴿By the fig and the olive, and by Mount Sinai, and by this secure city.﴾ The fig and the olive refer to the Holy Land from which the Messiah was sent, and in which the Gospel was sent down. Mount Sinai (Tur Sinin) is the mountain upon which Allah spoke to Musa, peace be upon him, speaking directly, and called him from the blessed side of the valley, from the blessed spot, from the tree within it. And He swore by "this secure city," which is Makkah, where Ibrahim settled Isma'il and his mother, and which is Paran as mentioned before. Since what is in the Torah is information about these, He mentioned them in chronological order, placing the earliest first, then the one after it. As for the Qur'an, He swore by it to honor its status and to show His power, His signs, His books and His messengers. So He swore by them in a graded order, step by step, beginning with the highest, then moving to what is higher than it, then higher still, for the most noble of the books is the Qur'an, then the Torah, then the Gospel. Likewise are the three prophets."

(Section)
What Ibn Qutaybah and other Muslim scholars mentioned is what whoever reflects upon the Torah will find expressly stated in it. In it is:

"Ibrahim rose early in the morning, took the boy, took bread and a skin of water, gave them to Hajar, placed them on her shoulder, and said to her: 'Go.' Hajar departed, and the water in her skin ran out. She cast the boy under a tree, and sat opposite him at a distance of a stone's throw, so that she would not see the boy as he died, and she raised her voice in weeping. God heard the voice of the boy, and where he was, and the angel said to her: 'Arise, lift up the boy and hold him with your hand, for I will make him a great nation.' God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water, so she gave the boy to drink and filled her skin. God was with the boy, and he grew up and dwelt in the wilderness of Paran."

This is the text of the Torah that Isma'il was raised and dwelt in the wilderness of Paran after he nearly died of thirst, and that God gave him drink from a well of water. It is known by mass transmission and the agreement of the nations that Isma'il was raised in Makkah, and that he and his father Ibrahim built the House. So it is known with certainty that Paran is the land of Makkah.

(Section)
Ibn Ishaq said: "Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah al-Ansari narrated to me, from men of his people, who said: 'What led us to Islam, along with the mercy and guidance of God, was what we used to hear from Jewish men. We were people of polytheism, worshippers of idols, and they were People of the Book, having knowledge that we did not have. There was always conflict between us and them. When we inflicted upon them something they disliked, they would say to us: "The time of a prophet who is about to be sent is near. We will follow him and kill you with him, a killing like that of 'Ad and Iram." We often heard this from them. When Allah, exalted is He, sent His messenger (ﷺ), we responded when he called us to Allah, and we recognized what they had threatened us with. So we hastened to him, believed in him, while they disbelieved in him. Concerning us and them these verses were revealed in al-Baqarah: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them, and before that they used to seek victory against those who disbelieved, but when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers.﴾"

In the Book of Isaiah: "I will praise My beloved and My son Ahmad." Therefore his mention appears in the prophecy of Isaiah more than in other prophecies. Isaiah openly proclaimed his name, his description, the description of his community, and called to it both secretly and openly, because he knew his rank and station with God, exalted is He.

Isaiah also said: "We have heard from the ends of the earth the voice of Muhammad." This is an explicit statement of his name (ﷺ). Let the People of the Book show us a prophet whose name, description, attributes, conduct, and the description and circumstances of his community were specified by the prophets, other than the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

The words of Habakkuk in his book: "God came from Yemen, and the Holy One from the mountains of Paran. The heaven was lit up by the splendor of Muhammad, and the earth was filled with his praise. The radiance of his appearance is like light. He surrounds his lands with might. Death marches before him, and the birds of prey accompany his soldiers. He stood and measured the earth, and the ancient mountains were humbled before him, and the hills sank down, and the walls of Madyan shook. He has gained the ancient glories." Then he said: "Your chastisement is in the rivers, and the thunder of your voice in the seas. You rode horses and mounted the chariots of the righteous. You will draw bows of tribes, and the heads will be quenched by your command, O Muhammad, with a full quenching. The mountains saw you and were terrified, and the torrent of rain turned away from you. The she-camels were distressed in anguish, lifting their hands in fear and dread. The armies marched in the flash of your swords and the gleam of your spears. The earth quakes and the nations are trampled, that you have appeared for the deliverance of your community and the rescue of the dust of your fathers."

Whoever seeks to turn this glad tidings away from Muhammad has sought to hide the sun by day and to cover the seas. How could he be able to do that, when he has described him with attributes that identify his person and removed the veil of confusion from the perplexed? Indeed, he explicitly named him twice, until the morning became clear to whoever has two eyes. He also informed of the strength of his community, of death marching before them, and of the birds of prey following their traces. This prophecy is fitting only for Muhammad (ﷺ), suits none but him, and descends only upon him. Whoever tries to divert the great rivers from their courses and to hold them back from their goal and their end, far-fetched is what the wrongdoers and deniers desire, "and God refuses except to perfect His light, though the disbelievers dislike it" (Qur'an 9:32).

Who is it whose community has filled the earth with their praise, and the praise of their community in their prayers and their sermons, and in the turning of their prayers, in ease and hardship, and in all states, other than them? So much so that God, exalted is He, named them "the praisers" before their emergence! And who is it whose face was such that the sun and the moon seemed to run within it from its brilliance and light?

He has accustomed the birds to habits, and they have become confident in him, so they follow him in every journey. Had he not said "I am a Messenger," would not the one who witnessed him see in his face one who speaks? And who is it whose death marched before him, and the birds of prey accompanied his soldiers, because they knew the nearness of the one who slaughtered the disbelievers for the One God, the Subduer?

They fly about him, offering their sacrifice with the blood of the disbelievers they have struck. And who is it before whom the mountains were humbled and the hills sank down, who trampled the nations and terrified the world, for whose prophethood the kingdoms were shaken, and who delivered the community from shirk, disbelief, ignorance, and injustice, equally?

The statement in the Book of Ezekiel, threatening the Jews and describing for them the community of Muhammad (ﷺ): "God will make them victorious over you, and will raise up among them a prophet, and will send down upon him a Book, and will give them dominion over your necks, so they will overpower and humble you justly. The men of the sons of Qedar will come out in multitudes of peoples, with them angels on white horses, armed, who will strike you down, and your end will be the Fire."

Who is it whom God made victorious over the Jews until He overpowered them, humbled them, struck them down, and sent down upon him a Book? And who are the sons of Qedar other than the sons of Isma'il, who went out with him, and who were multitudes of peoples? And who is it upon whom and upon whose community angels descended on white horses on the day of Badr, on the day of the Confederates, and on the day of Hunayn, so that they witnessed them with their own eyes, and he fought before them, on his right and on his left, until he defeated three hundred and thirteen men, who had with them only two horses, a thousand men clad in iron, counted among the cavalry of the Arabs, so that they became between slain, captive, and fleeing?

The statement of Daniel, mentioning him by his clear name without allusion or hint, and he said: "You will draw bows of tribes, and the arrows will be quenched by your command, O Muhammad, with a full quenching."

Also the statement of the prophet Daniel when Nebuchadnezzar asked him about the interpretation of a dream he had seen and then forgot: "You saw, O king, a great idol standing before you, its head of gold, its arms of silver, its belly and thigh of bronze, its shins of iron, and its feet of clay. While you were marveling at it, a rock came and struck that idol, and it crumbled and was reduced to dust, then the winds scattered it and it went away, and that stone turned into a great man who filled the earth. This is what you saw, O king." Nebuchadnezzar said: "You have spoken truly, so what is its interpretation?" He said: "You are the head which you saw of gold. After you, your son will rise, and he is the one you saw of silver, lower than you. After him there will arise another kingdom, lower than him, resembling bronze. After it, a strong kingdom like iron. As for the two feet which you saw of clay, it is a weak kingdom. As for the great stone which you saw strike the idol and crumble it, it is a prophet whom the God of the earth and the heavens will raise up with a strong law, who will break all the kings of the earth and their nations, until the earth is filled with him and his community, and his dominion will endure until the end of the world. This is the interpretation of your dream, O king."

It is well known that this applies exactly to Muhammad, son of 'Abdullah (ﷺ), point for point, and not to the Messiah nor to any other prophet. He is the one who was sent with a strong law, who broke all the kings of the earth and their nations, until the earth was filled with his community, and whose dominion is lasting until the end of time, which no one can remove, just as he removed the dominion of the Jews from the earth, and removed the dominion of the Christians from the best of the earth, its middle, so that it became in some of its outskirts, and removed the dominion of the Magians, the idol-worshippers, and the dominion of the Sabians.

The statement of Daniel also: "I asked God and humbled myself before Him to make clear to me what will happen to the Children of Israel, whether He will accept their repentance and restore to them their kingdom, and send them prophets, or make that among others. Then an angel appeared to me in the form of a young man of handsome face, and said: 'Peace be upon you, O Daniel. God says: The Children of Israel have angered Me and rebelled against Me, and worshipped other gods besides Me, and after knowledge they turned to ignorance, and after truth to lies. So I gave power over them to Nebuchadnezzar, who killed their men, took their children captive, destroyed their sanctuaries, and burned their books, and whoever came after him did likewise to them. I am not pleased with them, nor will I pardon their slips. They will continue in My wrath until I send My Messiah, son of the virgin pure one, and I will seal this upon them with the curse and wrath, so they will continue cursed, upon them is humiliation and poverty, until I send the prophet of the sons of Isma'il, of whom I gave good news to Hagar, and I sent to her My angel, and he gave her good news. And I will reveal to that prophet and teach him the names, and I will adorn him with piety, and make righteousness his emblem, and piety his inner nature, truthfulness his speech, fidelity his character, moderation his conduct, and rightness his way. I will single him out with a Book confirming what is before it of the Book, and abrogating some of what is in it. I will take him by night to Me, and raise him from heaven to heaven until he ascends, and I will bring him near, greet him, and reveal to him, then return him to My servants with joy and delight, guarding what was entrusted to him, truthful in what he was commanded, calling to My unity with gentle speech and good exhortation, neither harsh nor coarse, nor loud in the markets, compassionate to whoever befriends him, merciful to whoever believes in him, and stern toward whoever opposes him. He will call his people to My unity and worship, and inform them of what he has seen of My signs, and they will deny him and harm him.'"

Then Daniel recounted the story of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) as the angel dictated to him, until he reached the last days of his community, with the Blast and the end of the world. This glad tiding is now with the Jews and Christians; they read it and acknowledge it, and they say: "Its bearer has not yet appeared."

Abu al-'Aliyah said: When the Muslims conquered Tustar, they found Daniel dead, and they found with him a mushaf (codex).

Abu al-'Aliyah said: I read that mushaf, and in it was your description and your news, your conduct and the tones of your speech. The people of the region—meaning the people of the land of Suways where Daniel is buried—when they suffered drought, would uncover his grave and they would be watered. So Abu Musa wrote about this to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, and 'Umar wrote back to him: "Dig by day thirteen graves, and bury him by night in one of them, so that people are not tempted by him...."

Ka'b said: He mentioned the description of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in the Torah, meaning by "the Torah" that which is more general than the Torah in question: "Ahmad, My chosen servant, neither harsh nor coarse, nor loud in the markets, and he does not repay evil with evil, but pardons and forgives. His birthplace is Bakka, his migration is Taba, his kingdom is in al-Sham, and his community are the Praisers, who praise God in every high ground, glorify Him in every station, wash their extremities, wear their waist-wrappers at the middle, are the shepherds of the sun, their muezzin is in the air of the sky, their rows in battle and their rows in prayer are equal, monks by night, lions by day, and they have a hum like the hum of bees, and they pray the prayer wherever it overtakes them, even on a dunghill."

Ibn Abi al-Zinad said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith related to me, from 'Umar ibn Hafs, who was among the best of people, who said: My father and my grandfather had a leaf which they inherited before Islam, in which was the name of God, His true word, and the word of the wrongdoers in ruin. "This is the Reminder for a community that will come at the end of time, who gird their waists, wash their extremities, plunge into the seas toward their enemies. Among them is a prayer which, had it been among the people of Noah, they would not have perished by the flood, and had it been among Thamud, they would not have been destroyed by the Blast."

Isaiah, mentioning the story of the Arabs, said: "They will trample the nations as threshing floors are trodden, and affliction will descend upon the idolatrous Arabs, and they will be routed before drawn swords and bows bent taut from the severity of the battle." This is a report of what befell the idol-worshippers at the hands of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his companions on the day of Badr, on the day of Hunayn, and in other battles.

The statement in the Gospel which is in the hands of the Christians, from John: that the Messiah said to the disciples: "Whoever hates me hates the Lord. Had I not done among them works which no one else did, they would have had no sin; but now they have grown arrogant. The word that is in the Law must be fulfilled, for they hated me without cause. When the Paraclete comes, whom God will send to you from the Lord, the Spirit of Holiness, he will bear witness concerning me, and you also, for you have been with me from the beginning. I have told you this so that you will not doubt when it comes."

"Manahmana" in Syriac, and its interpretation in Greek is "Paraclete," and in Hebrew it is "the Praised One" and "the Praiseworthy," and "praise" as has already preceded.

The statement in the Gospel also: that the Messiah said to the Jews: "You say: 'Had we been in the days of our fathers, we would not have helped them to kill the prophets.' So complete the measure of your fathers, O serpents, offspring of vipers. How will you escape the punishment of Hell?"

This is confirmed by what occurs in Surah Ya Sin: "When We sent to them two, and they denied them both, so We strengthened them with a third."

That is certainly the case, that it came after the raising of the Messiah. The meaning of His words (and I will send to you prophets and scholars, and some of them you will kill and crucify, and some you will flog and hunt from one town to another, so that upon you will be completed the blood of the believers shed upon the earth, from the blood of the righteous Hābīl (Abel) to the blood of Zakariyyā ibn Barḍiyā (Zechariah son of Berekiah), whom you killed at the altar; all that I have described will surely come upon this nation. O Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you, I have wished to gather your children as a hen gathers her chicks beneath her wings, but you were unwilling. Behold, your house will be left desolate for you. I tell you, you will not see me from now until you say: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord) has already been discussed in tafsir (exegesis).

He informed them that they must fill the measure that had been decreed for them, and that He would leave their house desolate, meaning He would empty it of them, and that He would depart from them so that they would not see Him until the Blessed One comes, who comes in the name of God. He is the one who afterward avenged the blood of the believers. This is similar to His words in another place: "It is better for you that I go away, for if I do not go, the Paraclete (al-Bāraqlīṭ) will not come to you." And His words also: "The Son of Man is going, and the Paraclete will come after him." And in another place: "I am going, and the Paraclete will come to you."

The Blessed One who came after the Messiah is Muḥammad (ﷺ), as has already been established.

As for His words in the Gospel of Matthew: when Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā (John son of Zechariah) was imprisoned, he sent his disciples to the Messiah and said to them: "Say to him: Are you Elijah, or should we expect another?" The Messiah said: "Truly I tell you, there has not arisen among women anyone greater than Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā. The Torah and the books of the prophets follow one another in prophethood and revelation until John came. As for now, if you wish, accept it, for Īl (El) is about to come. Whoever has two hearing ears, let him hear."

This is good news of the coming of God, glory be to Him, who is called Īl in Hebrew. His coming is the coming of His Messenger, His Book, and His religion, as in the Torah: "God came from Mount Sinai." Some worshippers of the Cross said: "He only gave glad tidings of Elijah the Prophet."

This cannot be denied except out of the ignorance of a misguided nation and of worshippers of the wooden cross, which the hands of the Jews carved, for Elijah was sent many long ages before the Messiah.

As for His words in the prophecy of Jeremiah: "Before I created you, I honored you; before I formed you in the womb, I sanctified you, and I sent you and made you a prophet to all the nations." This is good news through the tongue of Jeremiah for one who would come after him, and it is either the Messiah or Muḥammad, may the blessings and peace of God be upon them both; it cannot refer to anyone other than them. Muḥammad is more deserving of it, because the Messiah was only a prophet to the Children of Israel, as God Most High said: ﴿and a messenger to the Children of Israel﴾.

The Christians acknowledge this, and the Messiah did not claim to be a messenger to the rest of the nations of the earth. The prophets from the time of Moses to the Messiah were only sent to their own peoples. Indeed, in the Gospel they have the saying that the Messiah said to the disciples: "Do not go into the way of the nations, but confine yourselves to the lost sheep of the house of Israel."

As for Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, God sent him to all the peoples of the earth and to all the communities of the children of Adam.

This good news corresponds with His words, Most High: ﴿O people, I am the Messenger of God to you all﴾.

And with the words of the Prophet (ﷺ): "I have been sent to the black and the red."

And his saying: "A prophet used to be sent to his own people, but I have been sent to all of humanity."

The Christians have acknowledged this good news and have not denied it. However, some of their leaders said that it is the good news of Mūsā ibn ʿImrān (Moses son of Amram), Elijah, and Elisha, and that they would come at the end of time. This is among the greatest slander, audacity against God Most High, and fabrication against Him, for one who has died will not come again until the appointed Day.

The saying of the Messiah in the Gospel that is in their hands, when he set forth the parable of this world, was: "It is like a man who planted a vineyard and fenced it around, placed in it a winepress, built a tower in it, entrusted it to laborers, and left it to be cared for. When the time of harvest drew near, he sent a servant to the laborers who were entrusted with the vineyard." Then he gave a parable for the prophets and for himself, and then for the prophet entrusted with the vineyard, another, until he made clear regarding his nation, and said: "And I tell you: the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a nation that is obedient and does good."

Then he gave the Children of Israel a parable of a rock, and said: "Whoever falls upon this rock will be broken, and whoever it falls upon will be crushed." This is the description of Muḥammad (ﷺ), and of whoever opposes and fights him among the people; it applies to no one after the Messiah except him.

The saying of Isaiah about his description: "Let the thirsty desert rejoice, and let the hills and wastelands exult, for it will be given, through Aḥmad, the excellence of Lebanon and the beauty of Dasākīr." By God, after this there is nothing but obstinacy and denial of the truth after it has become clear.

The saying of Ezekiel in his scrolls that are in their hands: God, Mighty and Majestic, says, after mentioning the disobediences of the Children of Israel and likening them to a vine that He nourished, "The vine did not remain long before it was uprooted in wrath and cast upon the earth, and the scorching winds burned its fruits. Then it was planted in the desert and in the neglected, thirsty land, and from its noble branches came out a fire that consumed that vine, until no strong branch or rod was found in it."

This is a clear statement, not an allusion, concerning him (ﷺ) and his land, which is Mecca, the thirsty, neglected land, deprived of prophethood before him since the time of Ismāʿīl.

As for what is in the scrolls of Daniel, who described the Kishdānīyyīn (Kashdanites), that is the Kildānīyyīn (Chaldeans), he said: "Their call will not waver, and the Lord has sworn by His arm that falsehood will not prevail, and no call of a false claimant will stand longer than thirty years."

The Torah contains something similar to this, and this is an explicit affirmation of the truth of his prophethood (ﷺ). For those who followed him after his death were many times more than those who followed him during his lifetime, and his call has passed over many centuries and remains established and continuous, and so it will remain until the end of time. This has never happened for any king, let alone for a lying fabricator against God and His prophets, a corrupter of the world, one who alters the call of the messengers. Whoever thinks this of God has thought the worst of Him and has impugned His knowledge, power, and wisdom.

I once had a debate with the greatest of those whom the Jews point to for knowledge and leadership. In the course of the discussion I said to him: "By your denial of Muḥammad (ﷺ), you have insulted God in the greatest insult." He was astonished at this and said: "Would someone like you say such a thing?" I said to him: "Listen now to its explanation. If you say that Muḥammad is a tyrannical king who subdued people by his sword and is not a messenger from God, and he remained twenty-three years claiming that he is the Messenger of God, sent to all creation, and saying: 'God commanded me to do this, forbade me from that, and revealed to me this,' while none of that was true, and he says that He permitted me to take captive the offspring and women of those who denied me and opposed me, to seize their wealth and kill their men, and none of that was true, and he is striving to change the religion of the prophets, to oppose their nations, and to abrogate their laws, then it is either that you say: God, glory be to Him and exalted, was aware of that, witnessing it and knowing it; or you say: it was hidden from Him and He did not know of it. If you say He did not know of it, you attribute to Him the worst ignorance, and then whoever knew it would be more knowing than Him. If you say, rather, that all of it was by His knowledge, His witnessing, and His awareness, then either He was able to change it, to seize the hands of the one doing it and prevent him from it, or He was not able. If He was not able, you have attributed to Him the worst incapacity, which contradicts lordship. If He was able, yet He still strengthens him, supports him, favors him, raises him, raises His word, answers his supplication, empowers him over his enemies, manifests at his hands a kind of miracle and marvel exceeding a thousand, and no one intends him harm without being defeated by him, and no one calls upon Him with a supplication without Him responding to it for him, then this is among the greatest injustice and folly, which it is not fitting to attribute to ordinary intelligent people, let alone to the Lord of the earth and the heavens. How, then, when He bears witness to him by affirming his call and supporting him by His speech? And this, by your reckoning, is a false and lying testimony?" When he heard that, he said: "God forbid that God would do this to a lying fabricator. Rather, he is a truthful prophet; whoever follows him prospers and is happy."

I said: "Then what keeps you from entering his religion?"

He said: "He was only sent to the unlettered (ummiyyīn) who have no book. As for us, we have a book that we follow."

I said to him: "You have been utterly defeated, for both the elite and the common people know that he announced that he is the Messenger of God to all creation, and that whoever does not follow him is a disbeliever destined for the Hellfire. He fought the Jews and the Christians, who are People of the Book. When his message is established, it is obligatory to believe in everything he reported." He fell silent and gave no answer.

Close to this debate was what happened to some scholars of the Muslims with some Jews in the lands of the Maghrib.

The Muslim said to him: "In the Torah that is in your hands today, God, Most High, said to Mūsā, peace be upon him: 'I will raise up for the Children of Israel a prophet from among their brothers like you; I will put My words in his mouth, and whoever disobeys him, I will take vengeance upon him.'" The Jew said to him: "That is Yūshaʿ ibn Nūn (Joshua son of Nun)." The Muslim said: "This is impossible for several reasons:

The first: in your own Torah, at its end, it says that there will not arise among the Children of Israel a prophet like Moses.

(The second): He said 'from among their brothers,' and the brothers of the Children of Israel are either the Arabs or the Romans.

For the Arabs are the sons of Ismāʿīl, and the Romans are the sons of ʿĪṣ (Esau), and these are the brothers of the Children of Israel. As for the Romans, no prophet arose from them except Ayyūb (Job), peace be upon him, who was before Moses, peace be upon him. So it is not permissible that he is the one the Torah gave good news of. Nothing remains except the Arabs, who are the sons of Ismāʿīl, and they are the brothers of the Children of Israel.

God Most High has said in the Torah, when mentioning Ismāʿīl, the forefather of the Arabs: that he would pitch his tent in the midst of the lands of his brothers, who are the Children of Israel.

This is good news of the prophethood of his son Muḥammad, who pitched his tent, and whose nation's kingdom is in the midst of the lands of the Children of Israel, which is al-Shām (Greater Syria), the place where his kingdom is manifest, as has already been mentioned in his saying: 'and his kingdom will be in al-Shām.'"

The Jew said to him: "But in the Qur'an you have: ﴿And to Madyan, their brother Shuʿayb﴾, ﴿And to ʿĀd, their brother Hūd﴾, ﴿And to Thamūd, their brother Ṣāliḥ﴾."

The Arabs say, "O brother of Tamīm," addressing one of them, so this is His saying: "raised up for the Children of Israel from among their brothers."

The Muslim said: "The difference between the two passages is clear, for it is absurd to say: 'the Children of Israel are brothers of the Children of Israel,' 'the Banū Tamīm are brothers of the Banū Tamīm,' or 'the Banū Hāshim are brothers of the Banū Hāshim.' This is something that no language of any nation would make sense of. Unlike your saying: 'Zayd is a brother of the Banū Tamīm,' and he is a brother of ʿĀd, and Ṣāliḥ is a brother of Thamūd, meaning one of them; so he is their brother in lineage. But if it were said: 'ʿĀd is a brother of ʿĀd,' 'Thamūd is a brother of Thamūd,' or 'Madyan is a brother of Madyan,' that would be a deficiency, and would be like your saying 'the Children of Israel are brothers of the Children of Israel.' So comparing one of the two passages with the other is clear."

The Jew said: "He informed that He would raise up this prophet for the Children of Israel, but Muḥammad was raised up for the Arabs and was not raised up for the Children of Israel. This specification implies that he was sent to them and not to anyone else."

Muslim said: "This is one of the proofs of his truthfulness, for he claimed to be the Messenger of Allah to the people of the earth, to both the People of the Book and the Unlettered (ummiyyin). Allah stated in the Torah that He would raise him up for them, lest it be supposed that he was sent only to the Arabs and the Unlettered. The Prophet (ﷺ) was specified by name because the addressee needed to be told of him, and lest the listener suppose that he was not intended by the general wording and not included in it, and to draw attention to the fact that others are more deserving of his ruling, and for other purposes. Thus, specifying the Children of Israel removes the illusion of one who supposed that he was sent only to the Arabs. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿So that you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you﴾, and these are his people, yet this does not negate that he is a warner to others as well. If you could cite from him that he claimed to be a messenger only to the Arabs, that would be a proof, but since his Book has spoken and both the elite and the common people know that he claimed to be sent to the Children of Israel and others, you have no proof."

The Jew said: "All our forefathers among the Jews agree that he claimed this. But the Isawiyya among us claim that he is the Prophet of the Arabs only, and we do not say what they say."

Then a Jew who was with him turned to me and said: "We have long been set in Judaism. By God, I do not know how to free myself from this Arab, but at the least, what we must oblige ourselves to do is to refrain from speaking ill of him."

Muhammad ibn Sa'd said in al-Tabaqat: Ma'n ibn Isa told us: Mu'awiya ibn Salih told us, from Abu Farwa, ... from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he asked Ka'b al-Ahbar: "How do you find the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the Torah?" He said: "We find him as Muhammad ibn Abd Allah, born in Makkah, emigrating to Taba, his kingdom in Syria. He is neither foul-mouthed nor loud in the markets, and he does not repay evil with evil, but he pardons and overlooks... "

Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi said: al-Hasan ibn al-Rabi' told us: Abu al-Ahwas told us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, who said: ... Ka'b said: "We find written in the Torah: Muhammad, neither harsh nor coarse, nor loud in the markets, nor does he repay evil with evil, but he pardons and forgives. His community are the praisers (al-hammadun) who glorify Allah on every high ground, and praise Him in every station; they gird their waists over their halves, and perform ablution up to their extremities. Their caller calls out in the atmosphere of the sky. Their rows in battle and their rows in prayer are equal. For them there is a humming like the humming of bees. His birth is in Makkah, his emigration to Taba, and his kingdom in Syria."

al-Darimi said: Zayd ibn Awf informed us: Abu Awana told us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Dhakwan Abi Salih, ... from Ka'b, who said: "In the first line: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, My chosen servant; neither harsh nor coarse, nor loud in the markets, nor does he repay evil with evil, but he pardons and forgives. His birth is in Makkah, his emigration to Taybah, and his kingdom in Syria. In the second line: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; his community are the praisers who praise Allah in every state and station, and glorify Him on every height. They are the shepherds of the sun, who pray the prayer when its time comes, even if they are on a dunghill. They gird their waists at their middles and perform ablution on their extremities, and their voices at night in the atmosphere of the sky are like the voices of bees..."

Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada said: ... from Namla ibn Abi Namla, from his father, who said: "The Jews of Banu Qurayza used to study the mention of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in their books, and they taught the children his description, his name and his emigration. When he appeared, they envied him, rebelled and transgressed..."

Abu Nu'aym mentioned in Dala'il al-Nubuwwa, from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Suhaym and Rumayh ibn Abd al-Rahman, both from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'id al-Khudri, from his father, who said: "I heard Abu Malik ibn Sinan say: I came one day to Banu Abd al-Ashhal to converse with them, and we were at that time in a truce of war. I heard Yusha' the Jew say: 'The emergence of a prophet called Ahmad is near, who will come out from the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram).' Khalifa ibn Tha'laba al-Ashhali said to him, as one mocking him: 'What is his description?' He said: 'A man, neither short nor tall, with redness in his eyes, wearing a shamla (wrap), riding a donkey, and this land is his place of emigration.'" He said: "I returned to my people, Banu Khudra, and I was that day wondering at what Yusha' said. I heard a man among us say: '(Does he alone say this?!) All the Jews of Yathrib say this.'" My father said: "So I went out until I came to the Jews of Banu Qurayza, and they discussed the Prophet (ﷺ). Zubayr ibn Bata said: 'The red star has risen, which has not risen except with the emergence and appearance of a prophet, and no one remains except that Ahmad's emigration is here.'"

Abu Sa'id said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in Madinah, my father told him this report, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'If Zubayr and his kinsmen, among the chiefs of the Jews, had embraced Islam, all the Jews would have embraced it, for they are merely followers of them.'"

al-Nadr ibn Salama said: Yahya ibn Ibrahim told us, from Salih ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, from Mahmud ibn Labid, ... from Muhammad ibn Maslama, who said: "There was not among Banu Abd al-Ashhal except one Jew called Yusha'. I heard him say, and I was a boy: 'The emergence of a prophet is near to you, who will be sent from the direction of this House.' Then he pointed with his hand toward the direction of the Sacred House of Allah. 'Whoever reaches him, let him believe in him.' Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent, and we embraced Islam while he was among us, but he did not embrace Islam, out of envy and rebellion..."

al-Nadr said: Abd al-Jabbar ibn Sa'id told us, from Abu Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Amiri, from Sulaym ibn Yasar, from Umara ibn Khuzayma ibn Thabit, who said: "There was no man among the Aws and Khazraj more descriptive of Muhammad than Abu Amir the monk. The Jews used to be intimate with him, and he would ask them about the religion, and they would inform him of the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and that this is the land of his emigration. Then he went out to the Jews of Taymaa, and they informed him of the same. Then he went out to Syria and asked the Christians, and they informed him of the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and that his emigration would be Yathrib. Abu Amir returned saying: 'I am upon the religion of the hanifiyya,' and he remained living as a monk, wearing coarse garments, claiming that he was upon the religion of Abraham and that he awaited the emergence of the Prophet (ﷺ). When the Prophet (ﷺ) went out and appeared, he did not go out to him, and he remained upon what he had been. When the Prophet (ﷺ) arrived in Madinah, he envied him, rebelled and became a hypocrite, and came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'O Muhammad, with what did you come? With what were you sent?' He said: 'With the hanifiyya.' He said: 'Do you mix it with other things?' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'I came with it pure and white. Where is what the rabbis of the Jews and the Christians used to tell you of my description?' He said: 'You are not the one they described.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'You lie.' He said: 'I have not lied.' The Messenger (ﷺ) said: 'The liar, may Allah cause him to die alone and expelled.' He said: 'Amen.' Then he returned to Makkah, and was with the Quraysh following their religion, and abandoned what he had been upon. When the people of al-Ta'if embraced Islam, he joined Syria, and died there, expelled, a stranger and alone."

al-Waqidi said: Muhammad ibn Sa'd al-Thaqafi told me, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd al-Aziz with a group, each told me a portion of the hadith, ... from al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba, that he entered upon al-Muqawqis, and said to him: "Muhammad is a sent Prophet, and if the Copts and the Romans obeyed him, they would follow him." al-Mughira said: "I remained in Alexandria, not leaving a church without entering it, and I asked their bishops, from among the Copts and the Romans, what they find of the description of Muhammad (ﷺ). There was a bishop among the Copts, who was the head of the Church of Abu Muhayyis, and they used to bring their sick to him and he would pray for them. I never saw anyone who did not pray the five prayers more diligent than him. I said: 'Tell me, is there any prophet still remaining?' He said: 'Yes, and he is the last of them; there is no one between him and Jesus. He is a prophet whom Jesus commanded us to follow; he is the Unlettered Arab Prophet, whose name is Ahmad, neither tall nor short, with redness in his eyes, neither white nor brown, letting his hair grow, wearing coarse garments, and content with whatever food he finds. His sword is upon his shoulder, and he does not care whom he meets. He engages in battle himself, and his companions ransom him with their own selves; they love him more than their children and their fathers. He goes out from the land of al-Qaraz, from a sanctuary to a sanctuary, emigrating to a land of salt flats and palm trees. He follows the religion of Abraham, girds his waist, washes his extremities, and is favored with what the prophets before him were not favored with. A prophet used to be sent to his own people, but he has been sent to all people, and the earth has been made for him a place of prostration and a purifier; wherever the prayer reaches him, he performs tayammum and prays. Those before them were restricted, and they would pray only in churches and synagogues...'"
