al-Tabarani said: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz told us: Abd Allah ibn Raja' told us: al-Mas'udi told us, from Fudayl ibn Hisham ibn Sa'id ibn Zayd, from his father, ... from his grandfather Sa'id ibn Zayd, that Zayd ibn Amr and Waraqa ibn Nawfal went out seeking the religion until they reached a monk in Mosul. He said to Zayd: "From where have you come?" He said: "From the House of Abraham." He said: "What do you seek?" He said: "I seek the religion." He said: "Return, for soon the one you seek will appear in your land." So he returned saying: "At Your service, in truth, in truth, in worship and servitude."

Ibn Qutayba said in Kitab al-A'lam: Yazid ibn Amr told me: al-Ala' ibn al-Fadl told us: my father told me, from his father Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sawiyya, ... from his father Khalifa ibn Abda al-Minqari, who said: "I asked Muhammad ibn Adi: 'How did your father name you Muhammad?' He said: 'Indeed, I asked my father what you asked me, and he said: I went out fourth of four men from Banu Tamim, I being one of them, with Sufyan ibn Mujashi' ibn Darim, Yazid ibn Amr ibn Rabi'a, and Usama ibn Malik ibn Jundub, intending Ibn Jafna al-Ghassani. When we came to Syria, we alighted by a pond with trees and a village of a monk, and he looked down upon us and said: "This language is not the language of the people of this land." We said: "Yes, we are a people of Mudar." He said: "From which of the Mudari?" We said: "From Khindif." He said: "Indeed, a prophet will soon be sent from among you. Hasten to him and take your share of him, and you will be guided, for he is the Seal of the Prophets, and his name is Muhammad." When we departed from Ibn Jafna al-Ghassani and returned to our families, every man among us had a boy born to him, and he named him Muhammad."

Imam Ahmad said: Rawh told us: Hammad ibn Salama told us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu Ubayda ibn Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from his father, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered the church, and there he found Jews, and a Jew was reading the Torah to them. When they reached the description of the Prophet (ﷺ), they stopped. At one side of it there was a sick man, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'What is the matter with you, that you have stopped?' The sick man said: 'They reached the description of a prophet and stopped.' Then the sick man came crawling until he took the Torah, and read until he reached the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and said: 'This is your description and the description of your community. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that you are the Messenger of Allah.' Then he died. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: 'Take care of your brother.'"

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 61, verse 6 (part 12 of 13):

Muhammad ibn Sa'd said: Muhammad ibn Umar narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Dawud ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, from his father, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them, ... from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: When Tubba' (a title of the kings of Yemen) came to Madinah and camped at Quba', he sent for the ahbar (rabbis) of the Jews and said: "I am going to ruin this town so that no Jewish community will remain in it, and the matter will return to the Arabs." Shamwal the Jew, who was then the most knowledgeable of them, said to him: "O king! This is a town to which the emigration of a Prophet from the descendants of Isma'il will be directed. His birthplace is Makkah, his name is Ahmad, and this is the abode of his migration. Your present dwelling will witness much killing and wounding among his companions and among their enemies." Tubba' said: "And who will fight him on that day, if he is a Prophet as you claim?" He said: "His people will march against him and they will fight here." He asked: "Where is his grave?" He said: "In this town." He asked: "If he is fought, to whom will the victory belong?" He said: "It will be his once and against him once. In this very place where you are, he will be defeated and his companions will be slain with a slaughter unlike any they suffered in any other place. Then the final outcome will be his, and he will prevail, and no one will dispute this matter with him." He asked: "What is his description?" He said: "A man who is neither short nor tall, with redness in his eyes, who rides a camel, wears a shamlah (a wrap cloth), and has his sword on his shoulder. He does not care whom he meets, whether a brother, a cousin, or an uncle, until his affair prevails." Tubba' said: "There is no way to this town for me, and its ruin would not be at my hands." Then Tubba' left and returned to Yemen.

Yusuf ibn Abd Allah ibn Salam narrated from his father: ... Tubba' did not die until he believed in the Prophet (ﷺ), because the Jews of Yathrib had been informing him of him, and Tubba' died as a Muslim. ...

Muhammad ibn Sa'd said: Muhammad ibn Umar narrated to us, Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, who said: Al-Zubayr ibn Bata was the most knowledgeable of the Jews, and he used to say: "I have found a book which my father kept hidden from me, in which there is mention of Ahmad: a Prophet who will emerge in the land of al-Qaraz, whose description is such-and-such." Al-Zubayr would narrate this after his father. The Prophet (ﷺ) had not yet been sent. When he heard that the Prophet (ﷺ) had emerged in Makkah, he deliberately went to that book, erased it, concealed the matter of the Prophet (ﷺ), and said: "He is not the one."

Muhammad ibn Amr said: Al-Dahhak ibn Uthman narrated to me, from Makhramah ibn Sulayman, from Kurayb, ... from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Jews of Quraytah, al-Nadir, Fadak and Khaybar used to find the description of the Prophet (ﷺ) with them before he was sent, and that the abode of his migration was in Madinah. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was born, the rabbis of the Jews said: "Ahmad was born tonight; this star has risen." When he became a prophet they said: "Ahmad has become a prophet; the star has risen." They knew this, acknowledged it, and described him, but what prevented them was only envy and rebellion. ...

Muhammad ibn Sa'd said: Ali ibn Muhammad informed us, from Abu Ubaydah ibn Abd Allah, and Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ammar ibn Yasir and others, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, ... from Aisha, who said: A Jew settled in Makkah, selling goods there. When the night came in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was born, he said in a gathering of the Quraysh: "Was there any child born among you this night?" They said: "We do not know of any." He said: "Look, O assembly of the Quraysh, and take account of what I tell you: the Prophet of this nation, Ahmad, has been born, and he has a birthmark between his shoulders, in which there are some hairs." The people dispersed from their gatherings, wondering at his speech. When they reached their homes, they mentioned it to their families, and it was said to some of them: "A boy has been born tonight to Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and he named him Muhammad." They came to the Jew at his house and said to him: "Did you know that a boy has been born among us tonight?" He said: "After my report, or before it?" They said: "Before it, and his name is Ahmad." He said: "Then go with us to him." So they went out with me until they came to his mother, and she brought him out to them. He saw the birthmark on his back, and the Jew (ʿfainted). When he recovered, they said: "What is wrong with you? Woe to you!" He said: "Prophethood has departed from the Children of Israel, and the Book has gone from before them. The Arabs have won prophethood. Are you rejoicing, O assembly of the Quraysh? By Allah, he will assault you with an assault whose news will travel from the east to the west." ...

Ibn Sa'd said: Ali ibn Muhammad informed us, from Ali ibn Mujahid, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Salim, the freedman of Abd Allah ibn Muti', from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to the House of Study (bayt al-midras, the Jewish place of learning), and said: "Bring out to me your most knowledgeable man." They said: "Abd Allah ibn Suriya." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took him aside and adjured him by his religion and by what Allah had bestowed upon them, and fed them with manna and quails, and shaded them with clouds: "Do you know that I am the Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes, by Allah, and the people know what I know, and your description and attributes are clear in the Torah, but they envied you." He asked: "Then what prevents you?" He said: "I dislike opposing my people. Perhaps they will follow you and embrace Islam, and then I will embrace Islam."

Abu al-Shaykh al-Asbahani said: Abu Yahya al-Razi narrated to us, Suhayl ibn Uthman narrated to us, Ali ibn Musahhir narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "I used to visit the Jews when they were studying the Torah, and I was amazed at the agreement of the Torah with the Qur'an and the agreement of the Qur'an with the Torah. They said: 'O Umar, no one is more beloved to us than you, because you visit us.' I said: 'I only come to be amazed at the Book of Allah confirming one part of it by another.' One day, while I was with them, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by. They said: 'This is your companion.' I said: 'I adjure you by Allah and by what He has sent down to you of the Book: do you know that he is the Messenger of Allah?' Their leader said: 'He has adjured you by Allah, so tell him.' They said: 'You are our leader, so inform him.' He said: 'We know that he is the Messenger of Allah.' I said: 'Then why do you destroy yourselves, if you know that he is the Messenger of Allah, and yet you do not follow him?' They said: 'We have an enemy among the angels and a peace-partner among the angels. Our enemy is Jibril, who is the angel of harshness and severity, and our peace-partner is Mika'il, who is the angel of compassion, mercy and gentleness. Jibril is his companion.' I said: 'I testify that it is not lawful for Jibril to be an enemy of Mika'il's peace-partner, nor for Mika'il to be an enemy of Jibril's peace-partner, nor to make peace with his enemy.' Then I stood up, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) met me and said: 'Shall I recite to you verses that have been revealed to me?' I said: 'Recite.' He recited: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Jibril – for he has brought it down upon your heart…﴾ [2:97]. I said: 'By Him who sent you with the truth as a prophet, I came only to inform you of what the Jews said.'" Umar said: "I became firmer in the religion of Allah than a rock."

Abu Nu'aym mentioned, from the hadith of Amr ibn Abasah, who said: "In the Jahiliyyah I turned away from the gods of my people, and I saw that they were worshipping stones on falsehood, which neither harm nor benefit. I met a man from the People of the Book and asked him about the best religion. He said: 'A man will come out from Makkah who will turn away from the gods of his people and bring the best religion. When you hear of him, follow him.' I had no concern except Makkah: I would go there and ask, 'Has any news happened there?' They would say, 'No,' and I would return to my family. I would also meet the riders and ask them, and they would say, 'No.' While I was sitting one day, a rider passed by me. I said: 'Where have you come from?' He said: 'From Makkah.' I said: 'Has any event happened there?' He said: 'Yes, a man has turned away from the gods of his people and calls to other than them.' I said: 'That is the one I am seeking.' So I saddled my mount, came, and embraced Islam. ..."

Abd Allah ibn Sa'id said: Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, and from Muqatil, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them: that eight of the bishops of Najran came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), among them al-Aqib and al-Sayyid. Then Allah the Most High revealed: ﴿Say: "Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, and ourselves and yourselves; then let us invoke Allah's curse upon the liars."﴾ [3:61]. They said: "Give us respite for three days." They went to the Banu Quraytah, al-Nadir, and Banu Qaynuqa', and consulted them. They advised them to make peace with him and not to engage him in mubahalah (mutual imprecation), and said: "He is the Prophet whom we find in the Torah and the Gospel." So they made peace with the Prophet (ﷺ) for a thousand garments in Safar and a thousand garments in Rajab, along with dirhams. Yunus ibn Bukayr said, from Qays ibn al-Rabi', from Yunus ibn Abi Salam, ... from Ikrimah: that some people of the People of the Book believed in Muhammad (ﷺ) before he was sent, but when he was sent they disbelieved in him. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿As for those whose faces turn black: "Did you disbelieve after your faith? Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve."﴾ [3:106].

Ibn Sa'd said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ya'qub al-Zam'i, ... from Sahl, the freedman of Uthmah, that he was a Christian and an orphan in the care of his uncle, and he used to read the Gospel. He said: "I took a mushaf (codex) of my uncle and read it until I came upon a page whose reading I found strange. It was stuck together, so I tore it apart and found in it the description of Muhammad (ﷺ): that he is neither short nor tall, white, with the seal of prophethood between his shoulders, who frequently retreats (for worship), does not accept charity, rides a donkey and a camel, milks the sheep, and wears a patched shirt. He is from the descendants of Isma'il and his name is Ahmad." He said: "My uncle came, saw the page, struck me, and said: 'What is your business with opening this page?' I said: 'In it is the description of the Prophet Ahmad.' He said: 'He has not yet come.' ..."

Wahb said: Allah revealed to Isaiah (Ash'ya): "I will send a Prophet by whom I will open deaf ears and veiled hearts. I will make tranquility his garment, righteousness his emblem, piety his inner nature, wisdom his understanding, dignity and truthfulness his character, pardon, forgiveness and kindness his disposition, justice his conduct, truth his law, guidance his leader, Islam his religion, and Ahmad his name. Through him I will guide after misguidance, teach after ignorance, multiply after scarcity, unite after division, and join together hearts that are different, desires that are scattered, and nations that are divided. I will make his community the best community, and they are the shepherds of the sun. Blessed are those hearts ..."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned, in the hadith of Uthman ibn Abd al-Rahman: ... that a man from the people of Syria, a Christian, came to Makkah, and passed by women who had gathered on one of their festival days, while their husbands were away on some of their affairs. He said: "O women of Tayma', there will be among you a Prophet called Ahmad. Whichever of you is able to become his bed, let her do so." Khadijah memorized his speech. ...

And ʿAbd al-Munʿim ibn Idris reported from his father, … from Wahb, who said, concerning the story of Dawud (David) and what Allah the Exalted revealed to him in the Zabur (Psalms): "O Dawud, there will come after you a Prophet named Ahmad and Muhammad, truthful and noble. I shall never be angry with him, and he will never anger Me. I have forgiven him before he angers Me, his past and future sins. His Ummah (community) is merciful. I shall give them supererogatory acts like what I gave the Prophets, and I shall make obligatory upon them the duties I made obligatory upon the Prophets and Messengers, so that on the Day of Resurrection they will come to Me with their light like the light of the Prophets before them. That is because I have made it obligatory upon them to purify themselves for every prayer, as I made it obligatory upon the Prophets before them, and I commanded them to perform Hajj as I commanded the Prophets before them, and I commanded them to fight in jihad as I commanded the Messengers before them. O Dawud, I have preferred Muhammad and his Ummah over the nations, just as I gave them six qualities that I did not give to any other nation. I do not hold them accountable for error and forgetfulness. Any sin they commit unintentionally, if they seek My forgiveness for it, I forgive them. For whatever they send forward for their Hereafter, given willingly, I hasten to them multiplied manifold, and for them with Me in the stored reward (al-madkhur) are manifold multiples, and better than that. I give them, for their calamities if they are patient and say 'inna lillah wa inna ilayhi raji'un,' blessings, mercy and guidance. If they call upon Me, I answer them. O Dawud, whoever of the Ummah of Muhammad meets Me testifying that there is no god but Me, alone, without partner, sincerely in it, he is with Me in My Paradise and My honor. And whoever meets Me having denied Muhammad, or denied what he brought, and mocked My Book, I shall pour punishment upon him in his grave, pouring it out, and the angels will strike his face and back when he is raised in his grave. Then I shall cast him into the lowest level of the Fire …"

And ʿAffan said: Hammam narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Zurarah ibn Awfa, … from Mutarrif ibn Malik, that he said: "I witnessed the conquest of Tustar with al-Ashʿari, and we came upon the grave of Daniel at Suways. Whenever they sought rain, they would go out and ask for rain through him, and they found with him a scroll. A Christian from al-Hirah called Nuʿaym sought it and read it, and at its bottom was: 'Whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers.' On that day forty-two rabbis embraced Islam among them, and that was during the caliphate of Muʿawiyah. So he presented them with gifts and gave them." Hammam said: Bistam ibn Muslim informed me that Muʿawiyah ibn Qurrah said: "We discussed the Book up to what it had become, and Shahr ibn Hawshab passed by us, so we invited him. He said: 'You have fallen upon one who knows. The Book was with Kaʿb, and when he was dying he said: Shall I entrust it to someone to deliver as a trust?' Shahr said: 'A cousin of mine, called Abu Labid, said: I will.' So he gave him the Book and said: 'When you reach such-and-such a place, board a qarqur (a ship) and then cast it into the sea.' He did so, the water parted, and he threw it into it. Then he returned to Kaʿb and informed him. He said: 'You have spoken truly. It is from the Tawrah that Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed.'"

[Section]

The questioner said:

"If you say that ʿAbdullah ibn Salam, Kaʿb al-Ahbar and others like them testified to this for us from their books, why did Ibn Salam and his companions who embraced Islam not bring their copies as witnesses against us?" The answer has several aspects:

First: The signs and proofs of prophethood are not limited to what the People of the Book possess regarding the description and attributes of the Prophet. Its signs are very diverse and numerous, and his description in the earlier scriptures is only one of them.

Most of the people of the earth did not embrace Islam on the basis of the proofs and reports in your books. Most of them do not know them nor have heard of them. Rather, they embraced Islam due to the proofs they witnessed and the signs they observed. Those proofs among the People of the Book came as reinforcement and support, in the sense of strengthening a structure, and the foundation was already complete without them. Thus the Arabs, from first to last, did not depend for their Islam on knowing what the People of the Book had of proofs, although that reached some of them and they heard it from them before and after prophethood, just as the Ansar used to hear from the Jews the description of the Prophet (ﷺ), his sending and his emigration. When they saw him and beheld him, they recognized him by the description the Jews had told them, and so they preceded them to him. Thus the enemies of Allah choked on their saliva and were choked by their water, and they said: "He is not the one we used to threaten them with."

Knowledge of the prophethood of Muhammad, Christ and Moses does not depend on knowing that those before them informed of and gave glad tidings of their prophethood. Rather, the ways of knowing it are many. Once the prophethood of the Prophet (ﷺ) is established by one of those ways, his prophethood is established and it becomes obligatory to follow him, even if it is not known that those before him gave glad tidings of him. If his prophethood is known through the proofs that establish it, then either the glad tidings of those before him concerning him are necessarily implied by his prophethood, or they are not. If they are not necessarily implied, then their occurrence is not obligatory, and the acceptance of the Prophet does not depend on them; rather, believing him is obligatory without them. If they are necessarily implied, it is known with certainty that they occurred, and their non-transmission to us does not indicate that they did not occur, since the existence of a thing does not entail its transmission, neither general nor specific. Not everything that Moses, Christ and other earlier Prophets reported has reached us, and this is known by constant experience. So even if it were supposed that the glad tidings of his prophethood (ﷺ) are not in the books that are in your hands, it would not follow that no one else gave glad tidings of him. It is possible that they are in books other than these famous ones circulating among you. There have always been books among every nation that only some of their elite know of, let alone all of their common people. It is possible that some of them contained it, then it was removed from them and altered, and copies of these altered ones were made and became widespread, so that no other is known, and the original copies vanished. All of this is possible, especially from a nation that colluded to change the religion and law of its Prophet. All of this is on the assumption that there is no glad tiding of him in any of their books at all. We have mentioned from the glad tidings of him in their books what they cannot deny or obstinately reject, even if they can deceive their ignorant and foolish people through interpretation.

The second aspect: ʿAbdullah ibn Salam confronted the Jews and agreed with them in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that his mention, description and attributes are in their books, and that they know he is the Messenger of Allah. They testified that he is their most knowledgeable and the son of their most knowledgeable, their best and the son of their best. Their statement afterward that he was their worst and the son of their worst, and their ignorant and the son of their ignorant, does not harm this testimony, just as when a witness testifies about a man before a judge, and the judge asks about him and he vouches for him, saying: "He is acceptable as a witness, just, trustworthy, who testifies only to the truth, and his testimony is valid against me." Then when he gives his testimony, he says: "He is a liar, a false witness." It is well known that this does not detract from his testimony.

As for Kaʿb al-Ahbar, he filled the world with reports of what is in the earlier prophetic scriptures about the glad tidings of him, and he declared them openly among the Muslims, the Jews and the Christians, and proclaimed them publicly. The Muslims among the People of the Book confirmed him in them and related to him what he reported, for he was the most knowledgeable of them in the books of the Prophets. The Companions used to examine what he transmitted and weigh it against what they knew to be sound, so they knew his truthfulness, and they testified for him that he was the most truthful of those who related to them from the People of the Book, or among the most truthful of them.

Today we stand in place of ʿAbdullah ibn Salam, and we have found these glad tidings in your books. They are a witness for us against you. The books are in your hands, so bring them and recite them if you are truthful.

Among us are those whom Allah has guided to Islam from among you, who agree with you, confront you and debate you on them. Otherwise, bear witness against yourselves to what Allah, His angels, His Prophets, His Messengers and His believing servants have testified against you: disbelief, denial, rejection of the truth and enmity toward Allah and His Messenger.

The third aspect: Even if ʿAbdullah ibn Salam brought you every copy containing the utmost clarity and explicitness, your obstinacy, stubbornness and lying would find in its faces and distort it in every way it could. When something comes to you that you cannot withstand, you say: "It is not that, and it has not come yet," and you say: "We do not depart from the ruling of the Torah, and we do not follow the Prophet of the Ummiyyin (the unlettered)." Your predecessors, who witnessed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and beheld him, explicitly stated that he was truly the Messenger of Allah, and that he is the one given glad tidings of and promised through the tongues of the earlier Prophets. Then some of them said to him to his face: "We testify that you are a Prophet." He said: "What prevents you two from following me?" They said: "We fear that the Jews will kill us." Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been decreed will not believe, even if every sign came to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾.

Signs have come to you that are greater and more manifest than the glad tidings of the Prophets concerning him, such that each one of them is enough for a human being to believe upon. Yet that only increased you in aversion, denial and refusal to accept the truth. Had He sent down to you His angels, had the dead spoken to you, and had every moist and dry thing testified to his prophethood, you would have been overcome by wretchedness and you would have gone to what was decreed for you in the Mother of the Book. Those among you who were wiser and further from envy saw the signs of the Prophets that they saw, and that only increased you in denial and obstinacy. Your predecessors and exemplars in denying the Prophets among the nations are beyond counting except by Allah, to the extent that it is as if you had agreed upon this, the first bequeathing it to the last, and the last following the first in it. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Thus did no Messenger come to those before them but they said, "A sorcerer or a madman." Did they bequeath it to one another? Rather, they are a transgressing people﴾. And suppose we set aside the reports of the earlier Prophets concerning him entirely: is there not in the signs and proofs that appeared at his hands what testifies to the soundness of his prophethood? We shall mention some of them after finishing the answers, a portion that cuts off excuse and establishes the proof. And Allah is the One sought for help.

(Section)

The verses of the Book have converged and the texts of the Sunnah have been widely transmitted in encouraging jihad and urging it, in praising its people, and in reporting what they have with their Lord of various kinds of honours and abundant gifts. Sufficient for this is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?﴾ [al-Saff: 10]

Souls longed for this profitable trade, to which the Lord of the worlds, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, pointed, so He said: ﴿You believe in Allah and His Messenger, and you strive in the way of Allah with your wealth and your lives﴾ [al-Saff: 11]

It is as if the souls were stingy with their lives and their survival, so He said: ﴿That is better for you, if you only knew﴾, meaning that jihad is better for you than sitting back for the sake of life and safety. It is as if they said: "What share do we have in jihad?" So He said: ﴿He will forgive you your sins﴾, along with forgiveness: ﴿and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow, and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence.
